The following changes were made: > Fixed Issues > > * Fixed an issue where, if a player disconnects and reconnects a controller, the game may not progress as normal. > * When this issue occurs, there are times when ghost data from Time Trials will be deleted without warning from "View Rankings." Differences from previous _Mario Kart_ games -------------------------------------------- ### Gameplay * Races now consist of 24 racers compared to the eight or 12 from previous games. * In races where the player travels along a [route](https://www.mariowiki.com/Route "Route"), including Knockout Tour, racers will automatically begin moving before the starting countdown, though [Rocket Starts](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rocket_Start "Rocket Start") can still be performed. * Getting hit by a car or train at certain angles causes the player to become unbalanced as opposed to spinning out. * Rather than using hang-gliders like in games since _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_, vehicles now use retractable wings to glide. * Several changes made in _Mario Kart 8_ have been reverted back: * [Lakitu](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lakitu_/(Mario_Kart_referee/) "Lakitu (Mario Kart referee)") has mostly been reverted to his pre–_Mario Kart 8_ behavior, where instead of immediately picking up a racer who falls off of a course, the screen will briefly fade to black before fading back in to him dropping the racer. However, Lakitu does appear briefly before the screen fades. * Players can once again receive a speed boost when being dropped off by Lakitu by pressing the drive button before hitting the ground when Lakitu drops them. * Falling off the course causes the player to lose their items. * Players can no longer see the items of other players (unless they are defensive items or Mushrooms). * If a racer falls off a course in the middle of a gliding section, Lakitu will place them back in the air so they continue gliding rather than bringing them to the nearest road. * Vehicles no longer [drive underwater](https://www.mariowiki.com/Underwater_driving "Underwater driving"), and instead continue along the surface of the water. * The traction stat is no longer visible on the vehicle selection screen. * Unlike in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, the [Mini-Turbo](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mini-Turbo "Mini-Turbo") boost charge thresholds when drifting are once again identical across all character and vehicle combinations, like they were in _Mario Kart Wii_, _Mario Kart 7_ and the Wii U version of _Mario Kart 8_. * The functionally distinct [sport bike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Sport_bike_/(vehicle_class/) "Sport bike (vehicle class)") vehicle class that existed in _Mario Kart Wii_ and _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ has been removed entirely. All bikes, regardless of their appearance or the rider's posture when riding them, are essentially considered to be [standard bikes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Standard_bike_/(vehicle_class/) "Standard bike (vehicle class)"), with the same drifting mechanics as all other vehicle types in the game. * The amount of coins a player can hold now caps off at 20, compared to the previous 10. * [Jump Boosting](https://www.mariowiki.com/Jump_Boost "Jump Boost") has been made more versatile: * It can now be performed multiple times in the air. * It can be performed at any time while gliding; tricking to the left or right will cause the racer to do a barrel roll. * It is now possible to trick off of other racers or obstacles by landing on top of them. * Racers can now charge up a [Charge Jump](https://www.mariowiki.com/Charge_Jump "Charge Jump"), allowing them to gain additional height, perform tricks, and gain speed boosts. * [Goombas](https://www.mariowiki.com/Goomba "Goomba") now charge towards racers when noticing them (similar to the 3D _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(series/) "Super Mario (series)")_ games), rather than simply walking in place or in a left-to-right pattern. * Explosions on the surface of water will create waves, which characters can trick off of. ### Controls ### Courses * Cups in Grand Prix are now based more on their region within the game's world map rather than following an overall difficulty progression across the game. * Unlike games since _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_, no race or battle courses from _[Mario Kart: Super Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Super_Circuit "Mario Kart: Super Circuit")_ return. ### Game Modes * By default, a Grand Prix now involves the first course of the cup being played with the multiple laps before subsequent races involve two-section routes leading into a full lap of a course for the final section. * In Time Trials, the game can be paused before the race starts. * VS Race and Battle mode options have several changes from _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_: * Teams can be set to No, Two, Three, or Four Teams instead of just No Teams or two teams with Team Game. * Items can only be set to Normal, Frantic, Mushrooms Only (as of version 1.2.0 and only for VS Race), or Custom Items (as of version 1.4.0). Shells Only, Bananas Only, Bob-ombs Only, No Items, No Items or Coins, and Skilled Items are no longer available. * Unlike in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, turning off every item in Custom Items in VS Race will no longer cause the Mushroom to automatically turn on. However, this does still occur in Battle mode. * COM Difficulty can be set to No COM in single player VS Race (as of version 1.2.0). * Setting COM Vehicles (between All Vehicles, Karts Only, or Bikes Only) is no longer available. * The "Choose" option in Course Selection has been renamed to "Open". * "In Order" is no longer available as a Course Selection option in VS Race and Battle mode. * VS Race's Race Count can be set to 3 (like _Mario Kart DS_, _Mario Kart Wii_, and the original _Mario Kart 8_) and 5 Races (like _Mario Kart DS_ and _Mario Kart Wii_), along with 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, and 32 Races still available. 24 and 48 Races are no longer available. * Battle mode's Round Count can be set to 3 Rounds (like the original _Mario Kart 8_), as well as 5 Rounds, along with 4, 6 and 8 Rounds still available. 10, 12, 15, 16, 20, 24, and 25 Rounds are no longer available. * Battle mode's Round Time is always 3 Minutes. Setting the Round Time from 1-5 Minutes is no longer available. * There is no longer a play stats menu. ### Items * [Mega Mushroom](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mega_Mushroom "Mega Mushroom"): * Racers under the effect of the Mega Mushroom item no longer shrink back to normal size when hit by Lightning. * After using a Mega Mushroom, the item slot shows the remaining time to be under the effect. As a result, the Mega Mushroom will count as being in use, so the player cannot use their other item nor receive another item if they already have two items, unlike in previous games where using the Mega Mushroom would remove it from the player's inventory immediately. * Like in _Mario Kart Tour_, the Mega Mushroom's theme from _[New Super Mario Bros.](https://www.mariowiki.com/New_Super_Mario_Bros. "New Super Mario Bros.")_ does not play while the item is in effect. * [Feather](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cape_Feather "Cape Feather"): * The Feather is now available in races, rather than being exclusive to Battle Mode. * Using the Feather item now allows racers to jump much higher and perform tricks after using it. * Feathers can now be dropped on the ground. * The player does not gain a speed boost upon landing after using a Feather unless they perform a trick after using it. * [Super Horn](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Horn "Super Horn"): * The Super Horn sound effect is identical across all characters, rather than being character-specific. * The Super Horn now stays in the item slot until it is fully used up. * [Star](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Star "Super Star"): * Stars can be found bouncing along the ground, as they do in the 2D _Super Mario_ games, in Free Roam. If a Star is dropped during a race, it will remain stationary, however. * A sound effect now plays indicating that the Star's effect is about to run out, similar to the mainline _Super Mario_ games. * [Lightning](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning "Lightning"): * The Lightning now only shocks players ahead of the user, rather than all opponents. * The Lightning now causes most players to be shrunk for the same amount of time, with racers in higher positions sequentially returning to their original size, similar to how it affected players prior to _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_. * The Lightning stuns players for longer when it first strikes, with each character having a unique animation for being struck. * Being under the effects of a Lightning does not cause the music to distort, similar to games prior to _Mario Kart DS_. * [Spiny Shell](https://www.mariowiki.com/Spiny_Shell_/(blue/) "Spiny Shell (blue)"): * The Spiny Shell now launches racers into the air at a higher angle, similar to its effect from _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_ to _Mario Kart Wii_. * Throwing the Spiny Shell has a slightly longer animation than throwing other items. * [Bullet Bill](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bullet_Bill "Bullet Bill"): * The Bullet Bill no longer causes players that it hits to spin out, instead causing them to get bumped out of the way and become unbalanced. * The Bullet Bill travels slower than before. * [Boo](https://www.mariowiki.com/Boo "Boo"): * The Boo item now applies a dithered transparency effect onto the user rather than turning them invisible, which is also applied to their held item resulting in them being invulnerable. * When using the Boo item, the user can now drive through off-road without slowing down, reverting to its behavior in _Mario Kart DS_. * When the Boo item steals from the player, like in _Mario Kart DS_, the Boo will hold the stolen item before leaving. When stealing the triple items, he will only hold one of the items. * When the Boo is in effect, the music and sound effects will be muffled. * [Fire Flower](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fire_Flower "Fire Flower"): * The Fire Flower now has a limit of eight fireballs, compared to the previous 10 in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ and _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_. * [Boomerang Flower](https://www.mariowiki.com/Boomerang_Flower "Boomerang Flower"): * The Boomerang Flower now has a time limit when using it and does not leave the item slot until it is fully used up, similar to the Fire Flower. This allows for it to be used up to four times, compared to the previous three in _Mario Kart 8_. * Items now float on the surface of water, rather than sinking. * Moving the camera with the right stick will aim items in that direction, with a full range of 360 degrees. * Due to 1st place being able to hold a ? Block and Coin at the same time (as of version 1.2.0), 1st place is no longer guaranteed to get at least one defensive item with Normal item rules when the maximum item slots are filled (outside of online rooms with high lag), like _Mario Kart 8_ for the Wii U, and unlike _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ and _Mario Kart Tour_ (when using three item slots). ### Aesthetic * Opening cinematics before races in the Grand Prix mode now show all of the courses at once before the first race, rather than each track individually at the start of each race. * The color of the sparks when charging an Ultra Mini-Turbo has been changed from purple to rainbow, similar to _[Mario Kart Arcade GP DX](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Arcade_GP_DX "Mario Kart Arcade GP DX")_. * Racers assume a horrified expression when they are about to be hit by a Spiny Shell. * Racers now brace themselves when tumbling, though they will still flail when spinning out. * The drivers of car obstacles are now visible. * The right stick can freely rotate characters and vehicles in the character and vehicle selection menu. Rotating in the vehicle selection menu will stop its automatic rotation. * The right stick can rotate cup trophies in the opposite direction of their automatic rotation. * Rather than being character-specific like in _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, vehicle horns are now vehicle-specific. * Vehicles' horns cannot be used after a race ends. * Vehicles briefly swerve left and right after spinning out. * A sound effect does not play when the player changes placement, similar to games prior to _Mario Kart Wii_. * Similar to _Mario Kart Tour_, a graphic appears on screen indicating that the player has either hit an opponent or has been hit during Battle mode. ### Music * The sped-up version of a course's theme during the final lap is only used when playing the course without routes in either Grand Prix or VS Race. In Knockout Tour, the sped-up version is also used for the final race. * Frontrunning beats do not play when the player is in first. * When approaching a course from a route, a simple transitional version of its theme can be heard before the main theme starts playing upon crossing the finish line. Staff ----- _Main article: [List of Mario Kart World staff](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_staff "List of Mario Kart World staff")_ _Mario Kart World_ is primarily developed by Nintendo EPD, with Kosuke Yabuki, Kenta Sato, Masaki Ishikawa, Shintaro Jikumaru, and Atsuko Asahi all returning from their respective roles from _ARMS_, another game led by the same team. In addition to Bandai Namco Studios returning to contribute to development, Monolith Soft and 1-Up Studio were also involved in the game's development. This game features neither [Shigeru Miyamoto](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shigeru_Miyamoto "Shigeru Miyamoto") nor series creator [Hideki Konno](https://www.mariowiki.com/Hideki_Konno "Hideki Konno") in lead development roles; only Konno receives a Special Thanks credit in the game. This is the first _Super Mario_ game to feature [Courtney Lin](https://www.mariowiki.com/Courtney_Lin "Courtney Lin") as the voices of [Peach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach "Peach") and [Baby Peach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Baby_Peach "Baby Peach"), [Laila Berzins](https://www.mariowiki.com/Laila_Berzins "Laila Berzins") and [Paul Castro Jr.](https://www.mariowiki.com/Paul_Castro_Jr. "Paul Castro Jr.") as the playable and non-playable [Toads](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad "Toad") respectively,[\[64\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-64) and [Laura Stahl](https://www.mariowiki.com/Laura_Stahl "Laura Stahl") as [Toadette](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toadette "Toadette"), following Nintendo's decision to recast their longtime voice actress, [Samantha Kelly](https://www.mariowiki.com/Samantha_Kelly "Samantha Kelly"). It is also the first game where [Kōji Takeda](https://www.mariowiki.com/K%C5%8Dji_Takeda "Kōji Takeda") replaces [Takashi Nagasako](https://www.mariowiki.com/Takashi_Nagasako "Takashi Nagasako") as the voice of Donkey Kong, reprising his role from the Japanese dub of _[The Super Mario Bros. Movie](https://www.mariowiki.com/The_Super_Mario_Bros._Movie "The Super Mario Bros. Movie")_, as well as the first game in the _Mario Kart_ series to feature [Kevin Afghani](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kevin_Afghani "Kevin Afghani"), [Giselle Fernandez](https://www.mariowiki.com/Giselle_Fernandez "Giselle Fernandez"), and [Dawn M. Bennett](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dawn_M._Bennett "Dawn M. Bennett") as the voices of their respective characters. Development ----------- "Mario Kart 9" redirects here. For the ninth _Mario Kart_ game released by Nintendo, excluding re-releases, see [Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour"). [![Image 646: Image of Mario from an early build of Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/e/e7/MKWorld_Early_Mario.png/220px-MKWorld_Early_Mario.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Early_Mario.png) Promotional prerelease art for Mario and the Standard Kart Prototyping for _Mario Kart World_ started in March 2017, with official work on the game beginning at the end of the year following the release of _[ARMS](https://armswiki.org/wiki/ARMS_/(game/) "armswiki:ARMS (game)")_, another game created by the same development team. The game was originally being developed for the [Nintendo Switch](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch"),[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart1-1) but it was moved to the Nintendo Switch 2 around 2020 following the conception of the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe_%E2%80%93_Booster_Course_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_.[\[65\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart2-65) _Mario Kart World_ is the first _Super Mario_ game since _[Super Paper Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Paper_Mario "Super Paper Mario")_ to be known to have been pushed back to a successor console. According to developers, had the game only introduced new courses and no new gimmicks, it would have likely been called _Mario Kart 9_; however, the open world gameplay was decided from the beginning, with the name _Mario Kart World_ already chosen very early in development.[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart1-1) [![Image 647: Concept artwork featuring Cow for Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/7/7c/MKWorld_Cow_Concept_Artwork_1.png/220px-MKWorld_Cow_Concept_Artwork_1.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Cow_Concept_Artwork_1.png) A sketch of [Cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") driving a truck, which the producers enjoyed The decision to include [Cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") as a playable character originated from a sketch done by one of the artists, featuring Cow driving a blue truck. The producers were so amused by the image that Cow was soon added as a playable character, which the developers named one of the "NPC drivers". Other obstacles soon became "NPC drivers" following Cow's addition, such as [Pokey](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pokey "Pokey").[\[52\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart3-52) The decision to increase the racer count to 24 came from one of the developers thinking that 12-player races would feel empty once the racers became spread out.[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart1-1) Glitches -------- ### Stuck Bomber Bill [![Image 648: A shrunken Bomber Bill seen in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/9/96/MKWorld_Bomber_Bill_Glitch.png/200px-MKWorld_Bomber_Bill_Glitch.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Bomber_Bill_Glitch.png) The shrunken [Bomber Bill](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bomber_Bill "Bomber Bill") on the left side of the road, shortly before disappearing If a [Banzai Bill Cannon](https://www.mariowiki.com/Banzai_Bill_Cannon "Banzai Bill Cannon") carried by a [pickup truck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pickup_truck "Pickup truck") shoots a [Bomber Bill](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bomber_Bill "Bomber Bill") inside of a [Knockout Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#Knockout_Tour "Mario Kart World") checkpoint, the Bomber Bill will briefly become stuck inside the checkpoint before disappearing. In this state, the Bomber Bill remains shrunken down as if it were still inside the cannon.[\[66\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-SirloinKnockout-66) ### Out-of-bounds shortcut In online races on [Whistlestop Summit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Whistlestop_Summit "Whistlestop Summit") and [Dandelion Depths](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dandelion_Depths "Dandelion Depths"), players can abuse the fact that [Lakitu](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lakitu_/(Mario_Kart_referee/) "Lakitu (Mario Kart referee)") will not pick up their COM-controlled character immediately after leaving a room.[\[67\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-67) On Whistlestop Summit, if a player jumps off to the right on the yellow rail after the long bridge and leaves the race before getting picked up by Lakitu, he will not pick up the COM-controlled character that races in place of the player, causing it to skip to the path below. On Dandelion Depths, if a player jumps off to the left of the road in the spiral turn and leaves the race before getting picked up by Lakitu, he will also not pick up the COM-controlled character that races in place of the player, causing it to skip to the end of the course's water section. If the glitch is done on the final lap, it will cause them a near guaranteed win unless first place is too close to the place where they end up after the shortcut. This is only useful in online lobbies during the last race due to the player's score resetting when they rejoin. ### Disabled Lakitu [![Image 649: A demonstration of the disabled Lakitu glitch in effect on the Rainbow Road track in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/85/MKWorld_DisabledLakitu.jpg/300px-MKWorld_DisabledLakitu.jpg)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_DisabledLakitu.jpg) [Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario "Mario") exploring an out-of-bounds area in [Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Rainbow Road (Mario Kart World)"). Note [Lakitu](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lakitu "Lakitu") attempting to pick up Mario; this animation would play continuously while the glitch was active. In VS Race or Time Trials, if the player selected any course, plugged in a single Joy-Con or Joy-Con 2 controller at the "OK" screen, and started the race or time trial with precise timing before the controller screen appeared, they would load into the course with the UI and race start timer sound effects missing. In this state, if the player entered an out-of-bounds area or fell off the course, they would not be picked up by Lakitu despite having the out-of-bounds animation play. This allowed the player to freely explore a glitched version of the game's map which lacked most objects and had non-functional [Warp Pipes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Warp_Pipe "Warp Pipe"). The player could exit this state by pausing the game, entering [Photo Mode](https://www.mariowiki.com/Photo_Mode "Photo Mode"), or swapping controllers. If the glitch was done on Rainbow Road, the course would be unloaded once the player respawned if they fell off it.[\[68\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-68) After ten minutes, the race or time trial is forced to end; if the Lakitu glitch was still active at this point, all menu options would cause the game to be unresponsive, forcing the player to close it via the HOME Menu. This could be avoided by disconnecting a controller before selecting a menu option. This glitch was fixed in the [version 1.4.1](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#Ver._1.4.1 "Mario Kart World") patch, released on December 15, 2025. Reception --------- _Mario Kart World_ received generally positive reviews. The departure from the traditional formula was praised, but certain aspects were considered shortcomings of the result of that direction. | Reviews | | --- | | Reviewer, publication | Score | Comment | | Scott Duwe, [Destructoid](https://www.destructoid.com/reviews/mario-kart-world-review/) | 9/10 | "_Mario Kart World is the latest and potentially greatest in the long-running arcade racer franchise, brought to the next level with the Nintendo Switch 2's hardware and an expansive roster of racers, tracks, and endless fun to be had. ._" | | Steve Watts, [GameSpot](https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/mario-kart-world-review/1900-6418371/) | 9/10 | "_Mario Kart World is a massive, sprawling sequel that playfully expands and iterates on the qualities that made Mario Kart 8 Deluxe such an enduring success. It's an incredibly fun and rewarding kart racing experience that's easy to understand, with enough mechanical nuance to reward veteran kart racers, all presented beautifully as a Switch 2 showpiece._" | | Logan Plant, [IGN](https://www.ign.com/articles/mario-kart-world-review) | 8/10 | "_Mario Kart World may not make the most convincing case that going open-world was the boost the series needed, but excellent multiplayer racing, incredible polish, and the thrilling new Knockout Tour mode still more than live up to its legacy._" | | Aggregators | | Compiler | Score | | Metacritic | [86](https://www.metacritic.com/game/switch/mario-kart-world) | ### Sales By June 30, 2025, _Mario Kart World_ had sold 5.63 million units worldwide, immediately becoming the best-selling game for the Nintendo Switch 2.[\[69\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-69) This meant the game had a 96% attach rate with sales of the Nintendo Switch 2 in the console's first month of availability. As of September 30, 2025, the game had sold 9.57 million units.[\[70\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-70) ### Awards and acknowledgements _Mario Kart World_ was nominated for two awards at [The Game Awards 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2025 "wikipedia:The Game Awards 2025"), in the categories "Best Family Game" and "Best Sports/Racing Game".[\[71\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-71) The game would go on to win "Best Sports/Racing Game", while _[Donkey Kong Bananza](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong_Bananza "Donkey Kong Bananza")_ won "Best Family Game" instead. It was also one of 30 games selected for the "Player's Choice" award, but failed to receive enough votes to make the top 10. [![Image 656: DK Spaceport](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/9/94/DK_Spaceport_view.png/250px-DK_Spaceport_view.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:DK_Spaceport_view.png) _[Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong_/(game/) "Donkey Kong (game)")_ (arcade) * [DK Spaceport](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Spaceport "DK Spaceport") is directly based on this game: * The course's structure is based on [25m](https://www.mariowiki.com/25m "25m"), being mainly comprised of an ascending sequence of zigzagging [girders](https://www.mariowiki.com/Girder "Girder") held by blue ladder-like support beams, with [Robo DK](https://www.mariowiki.com/Robo_DK "Robo DK") standing in for Donkey Kong. * Obstacles include giant rolling [barrels](https://www.mariowiki.com/Barrel "Barrel") and [oil drums](https://www.mariowiki.com/Oil_drum "Oil drum") (based on their design from this game) with nearby [Fire Snakes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fire_Snake "Fire Snake") in place of [Fireballs](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fireball_/(Donkey_Kong/) "Fireball (Donkey Kong)"). Stacks of these barrels can also be found at the top of the course corresponding to the location where [Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong "Donkey Kong") would take his barrels from in 25m. * The course's decorations reference _Donkey Kong_ iconography, including warning posters depicting the sprites of fireballs, oil drums, and barrels; a poster based on the "How high can you get?" screen; pixelated paintings of Donkey Kong's face on [ramps](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ramp "Ramp"); and stylized neon illustrations of oil drums, upright and rolling barrels, [hammers](https://www.mariowiki.com/Hammer "Hammer"), [Fires](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fire_/(enemy/) "Fire (enemy)"), [Pauline's Parasol and Bag](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pauline%27s_lost_items "Pauline's lost items"), and the 300 [points](https://www.mariowiki.com/Point "Point") for collecting them. The illustrations of Fires are either orange and yellow or cyan and magenta, which are the colors they originally appeared in. * The room past the finish line features arcade-inspired elements such as a "high score" message above the exit archway and a circuit board incorporated into the ceiling. * The course's music primarily consists of variations of "[Round 1 BGM](https://www.mariowiki.com/Round_1_BGM_/(Donkey_Kong/) "Round 1 BGM (Donkey Kong)")", with the "[Round Start BGM](https://www.mariowiki.com/Round_Start_BGM?action=edit&redlink=1 "Round Start BGM (page does not exist)")" and "[Game Start](https://www.mariowiki.com/Game_Start_/(Donkey_Kong/) "Game Start (Donkey Kong)")" jingles being incorporated as brass licks. Rather than a final lap variation, this track instead features an arrangement of "[Hammer BGM](https://www.mariowiki.com/Hammer_BGM "Hammer BGM")". "Round 1 BGM" is also incorporated into the music played during DK Spaceport's pre-race, and the [coda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coda_/(music/) "wikipedia:Coda (music)") used in Knockout Tour uses the "Round 1 and 2 Clear" jingle. * The sound effect played when a racer is bounced by a Donkey Kong-branded [trampoline](https://www.mariowiki.com/Trampoline "Trampoline") is based on the one heard when accruing points in this game, like when jumping over barrels. * Completing the [mission](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_missions "List of Mario Kart World missions") "Remember the classic DONKEY KONG!" awards a [sticker](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_stickers_in_Mario_Kart_World "List of stickers in Mario Kart World") depicting Donkey Kong's sprite. Completing the mission "Race to get ahead of the explosives!" awards a sticker depicting a Fireball's sprite. Stickers depicting Donkey Kong grinning and frowning are awarded for driving three hundred twenty kilometers and gliding for forty kilometers respectively. Stickers depicting the oil drum's sprite and the neon illustrations of the hammer and Pauline's Parasol from DK Spaceport can be awarded. _[Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong_/(Game_%26_Watch/) "Donkey Kong (Game & Watch)")_ (Game & Watch) * The starting banner in DK Spaceport is based on the Donkey Kong Game & Watch unit, and directional pad iconography is seen throughout the course and on Robo DK's back. _[Mario Bros.](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Bros._/(game/) "Mario Bros. ["This Is It!" - Nintendo On Why It Added 'Cow' Into Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/news/2025/05/this-is-it-nintendo-on-why-it-added-cow-into-mario-kart-world)
============================================================================================================================================================================================

What an udder surprise

*   ![Image 2: Olliemar28](https://images.nintendolife.com/users/61767/avatar.jpg?v=1687185714)
*   by [Ollie Reynolds](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/authors/Olliemar28) Wed 21st May 2025

[![Image 3: MK World - Cow 2](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.900x.jpg)](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.large.jpg "MK World - Cow 2")

_Image: Nintendo_

If you watched any of the reactions to the [Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/games/nintendo-switch-2/mario-kart-world) reveal trailer, then chances are you saw somebody loudly exclaim "you can play as a _COW?!"_.

Yes, the cow, an NPC character known for its presence in Moo Moo Meadows, is now playable in the upcoming Mario Kart tile for Switch 2. In the recent [Ask the Developer](https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-3/) interview over at Nintendo, Masaaki Ishikawa explained the reasoning behind Cow's inclusion.

Honestly, it seems to have simply been a case of pondering what new additions could be added after Mario Kart 8 Deluxe included so many newcomers. Here's what Ishikawa had to say:

> "Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that's when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> "The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn't feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world."

Characters such as Cow and Cheep Cheep are known as 'NPC Racers' within Nintendo, with Ishikawa joking that Cow in particular "is actually a pivotal character in the Mario Kart series".

To coincide with the information from the Ask the Developer interview, Nintendo has also released new footage from Mario Kart World showcasing Cow taking part in one of the game's missions, as shown by [TodayNews on BlueSky.](https://bsky.app/profile/today.oatmealdome.me/post/3lpousecsiy2c) The task? "Mooove" through a herd of cows, of course. Chortle!

> 📰 \[Mario Kart™ World\] P Switch Mission #1 View this content in the Nintendo Today! app: 🔗 today.oatmealdome.me
> 
> — [TodayNews (@today.oatmealdome.me)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:aukx63w54rzwuev74z5qxngk?ref_src=embed) [2025-05-21T15:05:01.2530682Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:aukx63w54rzwuev74z5qxngk/post/3lpousecsiy2c?ref_src=embed)

Mario Kart World is scheduled to launch alongside the Switch 2 on **5th June 2025**. Nintendo also revealed that the game was originally in development for Switch 1, and also explained why it chose not to call the game 'Mario Kart 9'.

Model from _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ |
| **First appearance** | _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_ ([1996](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#1996 "List of games by date")) |
| **Latest appearance** | _[Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Party_Jamboree_%E2%80%93_Nintendo_Switch_2_Edition_%2B_Jamboree_TV "Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV")_ ([2025](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#2025 "List of games by date")) |

**Cows** (also referred to as **Moo Moos**)[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) appear as a recurring species in the [_Super Mario_ franchise](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)"), first appearing in _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_. They are primarily associated with farm-based courses in the _[Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart "Mario Kart")_ series, in which they typically act as obstacles.

History\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")\]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### _Mario Kart_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mario Kart series")\]

#### _Mario Kart 64_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mario Kart 64")\]

[![Image 2: Moo Moo Farm from Mario Kart 64.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/e/e3/Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png/200px-Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)

Cows can be seen in the background of the _Mario Kart 64_ course [Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm").

#### _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")\]

Although cows themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Double_Dash!! "Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")_, [Mushroom City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_City "Mushroom City") has a truck advertising the Moo Moo Farm course with the image of a cow.

#### _Mario Kart DS_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mario Kart DS")\]

In _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_, cows once again appear in the background of [N64 Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm"). It is the first game to give them the blue collars with hanging golden bells.

#### _Mario Kart Wii_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mario Kart Wii")\]

[![Image 3: A cow in MKW](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/6/60/MushroomCow.png/140px-MushroomCow.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MushroomCow.png)

A Moo Moo as seen in _Mario Kart Wii_

In _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_, cows serve as obstacles in the course [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows"). When hit, they cause the player to spin out. While the ones seen up close use full models, some in the distant background reuse flat textures from _Mario Kart DS_. A truck in the [Moonview Highway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moonview_Highway "Moonview Highway") course also has a picture of a cow printed on it with the text "[Moo Moo Dairy](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_Wii#Moo_Moo_Dairy "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart Wii")".

#### _Mario Kart 7_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Mario Kart 7")\]

Two cows make a small appearance in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ on a sign in the [Wii Coconut Mall](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coconut_Mall "Coconut Mall") course, which reads "Moo Moo Dairy".

#### _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Mario Kart 8 / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")\]

Moo Moos return in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ with the return of the Moo Moo Meadows track, with some Moo Moos now having other colors, such as solid black or brown. Also, in [Toad Harbor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad_Harbor "Toad Harbor") and the game's rendition of [Toad's Turnpike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Turnpike "Toad's Turnpike"), there are advertising trucks and signs with Moo Moos on them. There is also a sponsor known as [Moo Moo Meadows Milk](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_8_and_Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe#Moo_Moo_Meadows_Milk "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart 8 and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe"). In this game, Moo Moos appear in four different colors; white with blue spots, white with brown spots, black, or brown. The Mii Racing Suit based on a Moo Moo appears in the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe_%E2%80%93_Booster_Course_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_.

#### _Mario Kart Tour_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mario Kart Tour")\]

[![Image 4: The Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit from Mario Kart Tour](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/c/c0/MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png/60px-MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor returns in several courses in the game, and the [Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") and [Moo Moo Offroader](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Offroader "Moo Moo Offroader") are both based on them and were introduced in the [Animal Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Animal_Tour "Animal Tour").

#### _Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")\]

In _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, the [Windmill Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Windmill_Meadows "Windmill Meadows") features some Moo Moos as obstacles.

#### _Mario Kart World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mario Kart World")\]

[![Image 5: Cow in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/3/37/MKWMooMoo.jpg/200px-MKWMooMoo.jpg)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWMooMoo.jpg)

Cow racing in _Mario Kart World_.

In _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_, cows return as obstacles on Moo Moo Meadows. In addition, a cow appears as a playable character for the first time in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ franchise as a whole. Her [emblem](https://www.mariowiki.com/Emblem "Emblem") consists of a stylized depiction of her face. Moo Moo Meadows also now features a large golden statue of a cow on a bike.

The playable cow is unlockable in version 1.0.0, but made available from the start following a software update. She is a heavyweight character, sharing statistics with [Wario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario "Wario"), [Waluigi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi "Waluigi"), [Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong "Donkey Kong"), [Wiggler](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wiggler "Wiggler"), [Chargin' Chuck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chargin%27_Chuck "Chargin' Chuck"), and [Pianta](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pianta "Pianta").

Missions

Cows are featured in the following [missions](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_missions "List of Mario Kart World missions") in _Mario Kart World_:

| Mission | Location | Time limit (seconds) | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [![Image 6: Mario Kart World P-Switch Mission "Moove through the herd of cows!"](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/f/f8/Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png/200px-Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png)  
_Mooove through the herd of cows!_ | [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows") | 15.00 | The player must maneuver through a large crowd of cows and reach the goal ring in time. |

### _Mario Party_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Mario Party series")\]

Moo Moos make four background appearances in the [_Mario Party_ series](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_/(series/) "Mario Party (series)"). They appear in the background of [Western Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Western_Land "Western Land") in _[Mario Party 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_2 "Mario Party 2")_ and _[Super Mario Party Jamboree](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Party_Jamboree "Super Mario Party Jamboree")_ and [Fowl Play](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fowl_Play "Fowl Play") in _[Mario Party 3](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_3 "Mario Party 3")_, and in _[Mario Party: Island Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party:_Island_Tour "Mario Party: Island Tour")_, they appear on [Perilous Palace Path](https://www.mariowiki.com/Perilous_Palace_Path "Perilous Palace Path").

### _Mario Pinball Land_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Mario Pinball Land")\]

In _[Mario Pinball Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Pinball_Land "Mario Pinball Land")_, there is a rare chance for a Moo Moo to pop out of a hole by hitting a [Monty Mole](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole"). If [Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario "Mario") hits the Moo Moo before it disappears, he gains 100,000 [points](https://www.mariowiki.com/Point "Point").

### _Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games")\]

Cows reappear in _[Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_%26_Sonic_at_the_London_2012_Olympic_Games_/(Wii/) "Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games (Wii)")_ on Moo Moo Meadows as obstacles in the [Dream Equestrian](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dream_Equestrian "Dream Equestrian") event.

### _Yoshi_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Yoshi series")\]

#### _Yoshi's Woolly World_ / _Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Yoshi's Woolly World / Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")\]

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "Yoshi's Woolly World")_ and _[Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Poochy_%26_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")_, Moo Moo Yoshi is available as an unlockable Yoshi [pattern](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Yoshi_designs_in_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "List of Yoshi designs in Yoshi's Woolly World") which resembles a Moo Moo.

#### _Yoshi's Crafted World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Yoshi's Crafted World")\]

In _[Yoshi's Crafted World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "Yoshi's Crafted World")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor from _Mario Kart 8_ makes various cameo appearances on the cartons and signs in the background of the flip side of [Rail-Yard Run](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rail-Yard_Run "Rail-Yard Run") and [Go-Go Yoshi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Go-Go_Yoshi "Go-Go Yoshi"). As first seen on the front side of Rail-Yard Run, there are also five cardboard Cow [crafts](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_crafts_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of crafts in Yoshi's Crafted World"), which serve as [Coal Blockafeller](https://www.mariowiki.com/Blockafeller "Blockafeller")'s first souvenir request. There is additionally a Cow [costume](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_costumes_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of costumes in Yoshi's Crafted World") for Yoshi to wear.

### Other appearances\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Other appearances")\]

#### _Nintendo Badge Arcade_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Nintendo Badge Arcade")\]

Cows[\[3\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) appear as badges in _[Nintendo Badge Arcade](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nintendo_Badge_Arcade "Nintendo Badge Arcade")_ that the player may collect and decorate their Nintendo 3DS HOME Menu with. They are a part of the _Mario Kart 8_ set of badges.

#### _Minecraft_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Minecraft")\]

In the Super Mario Mash-Up Pack in _[Minecraft](https://www.mariowiki.com/Minecraft "Minecraft")_, the traditional [Cow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Cow "minecraftwiki:Cow")'s design is replaced with the Moo Moo design found in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ titles. Red and green Moo Moos with mushrooms on their back replace Mooshrooms.

Gallery\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Gallery")\]
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Naming\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Naming")\]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The name "Cow" (capitalized as such) is used in-game in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_. Prior to this, supplementary material variously referred to them as "cows" (in lowercase)[\[4\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4)[\[5\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-7)[\[3\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) or "Moo Moos"[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) (alternatively lowercased as "moo moos"),[\[4\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4) with the latter being primarily used by third-party guidebooks. Though the name "Moo Moo" has never been explicitly used to refer to them in-game, it is implied in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ by the name of the Moo Moo [Mii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") Racing Suit.

"I have this memory of approving the concept for Cow, and then maybe the next day I had 10 proposals for other characters on my desk."
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

After spending the last 30 years grazing the fields of Moo Moo Farm and Moo Moo Meadows, [Cow has taken the spotlight](https://www.ign.com/articles/you-can-play-as-the-moo-moo-meadows-cow-in-mario-kart-world-and-the-internet-is-thrilled) as the biggest breakout star of Mario Kart World's enormous character roster. So when Nintendo invited us to a roundtable interview with Mario Kart World Producer Kosuke Yabuki, we knew we had to ask him about the beloved bovine.

"Thank you for that question about Cow," Yabuki began, which is one of the best openings I've ever heard in an interview. "The decision to include Cow was something that we considered in terms of if we added that, I think people would be really happy about it. And so we did. But honestly, the reaction to that by the public was much bigger than we possibly could have anticipated. So that was a wonderful surprise. Thank you."

Yabuki's surprise at Cow's popularity matches what we heard from Nintendo of America's Bill Trinen, [who told us in an interview](https://www.ign.com/articles/our-big-nintendo-switch-2-interview-with-nintendo-of-americas-bill-trinen) that their internal expectations for Cow were "perhaps not as big as the cow has become."

Cow's origin story makes her inclusion even better. In last month's Ask the Developer series about Mario Kart World, Yabuki confirmed that it was [a developer's "silly sketch" of Cow driving a truck](https://www.ign.com/articles/nintendo-reveals-silly-sketch-of-mario-kart-world-cow-that-led-to-the-games-best-new-character-becoming-playable) that convinced him and the rest of the team to add Cow as a playable character. I asked Yabuki about the evolution during development of what they're now calling "NPC Drivers", which grew to include characters like Snowman, Penguin, Swooper, and many others.

"I have to say, adding in Cow really opened the floodgates for us because once you've got a character in like that, you start to think, 'well, maybe we should just add who we can,'" Yabuki continued. "And so that was the point at which the designers got really excited. Once they realized all of these characters were possibly up for grabs, that's when you start to see Penguin come in, Pokey comes in, one after another, these new designs for characters keep coming. And so because all of these characters came in such a rush as the designers were getting kind of carried away, it's actually a little hard for me to remember which specific character would've come immediately next in the sequence after Cow. Sorry about that! Because honestly, I have this memory of approving the concept for Cow, and then maybe the next day I had 10 proposals for other characters on my desk."

... adding in Cow really opened the floodgates for us.

There's a potential darker side to this story, too, as one of Mario Kart World's other new additions is Dash Food, which characters pick up from Yoshi's drive-thrus around the open world. Shortly after Mario Kart World was unveiled, IGN's Brian Altano noticed at a preview event that [Cow was able to eat products that traditionally include beef](https://www.ign.com/articles/yes-mario-kart-worlds-cow-can-eat-burgers-and-steak), like steak kabobs and hamburgers. So, we asked Yabuki the ultimate question: Are those veggie burgers, or what's going on there?

> Yes, Cow CAN eat steak in Mario Kart World. [pic.twitter.com/qN5PZ9IIM4](https://t.co/qN5PZ9IIM4)
> 
> — IGN (@IGN) [April 4, 2025](https://twitter.com/IGN/status/1908259261769003473?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

"Sorry, that's top secret," Kabuki said with a laugh. "I can't say."

Well, the mystery remains, as does the question of [if Diddy Kong will appear in Mario Kart World sporting his new redesign](https://www.ign.com/articles/after-redesigning-donkey-kong-nintendo-has-tweaked-another-classic-character-and-heres-our-best-look-yet), to which Yabuki simply said, "I'm afraid I can't say anything at this time." But the rest of Mario Kart World's mysteries will soon be solved, as we're just two days away from the release date of Nintendo Switch 2 and its flagship launch game. For more, check out our [final hands-on preview of Mario Kart World](https://www.ign.com/articles/mario-kart-world-the-final-preview), where we were impressed with the racing, but still haven't been sold on Free Roam. And, check out our [preview of that $10 launch game, Nintendo Switch 2 Welcome Tour](https://www.ign.com/articles/nintendo-switch-2-welcome-tour-so-is-it-worth-10).

![Image 1: Mario Kart World (Video Game)](https://mediaproxy.tvtropes.org/width/1200/https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/1000000185.png)

_Mario Kart World_ is a 2025 [mascot racer](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MascotRacer "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MascotRacer") video game and the 10th installment of the _[Mario Kart](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart")_ series. It was released on June 5th, 2025 for the [Nintendo Switch 2](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Platform/NintendoSwitch2 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Platform/NintendoSwitch2") as a launch title.

Introduced in this entry is the titular "Mario Kart World'', where all of the race tracks now exist in a massive, interconnected world. Taking advantage of this are the new Knockout Tour and Free Mode modes: the former consists of a series of [elimination races](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlayerElimination "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlayerElimination") where players race through world's interconnected routes, with brief passes by of the main courses serving as checkpoints where the bottom four are eliminated, while the latter allows players to explore the game's world at their own leisure, or take on activities like doing P-Switch challenges, collecting Peach Medallions, and hitting ? Switches that award you stickers to decorate your kart.

The open world experience also extends to the main Grand Prix, as after the first race, you'll find that the subsequent races now have you and the other drivers take to the highways, waterways, off-road, and more to get to the next course. Thanks to the hundreds of interconnecting routes that you'll see across the game's different modes, _Mario Kart World_'s soundtrack includes over 200 new arrangements of songs to accompany you whether you're racing from coast-to-coast or on a casual drive through the countryside, remixing and reimagining tracks from across the wider _[Super Mario Bros.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Franchise/SuperMarioBros "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Franchise/SuperMarioBros")_ franchise: ranging from other _Mario Kart_ games, to the mainline platformers, to spin-offs like _[Yoshi's Story](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/YoshisStory "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/YoshisStory")_ and _[WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/WarioWareIncMegaMicrogames "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/WarioWareIncMegaMicrogames")_, to even surprising choices like the "The Mario Drawing Song" from _Flipnote Studio_.

Other significant changes to the gameplay are races now featuring 24 characters at once, the first increase in driver count since _[Mario Kart Wii](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii")_; an expanded trick system that allows the player to rail grind, wall ride, and charge jump all over the environment to cut corners and find alternate paths; and the removal of underwater driving in favor of your kart transforming into a boat to ride the waves (and of lesser consequence, your glider has now been swapped out in favor of plane wings). Character costumes also return from _[Mario Kart Tour](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour")_, though new outfits are now gained by grabbing a bag of location-themed "Dash Food" at roadside eateries during races and in Free Roam.

*   [Abandoned Laboratory](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AbandonedLaboratory "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AbandonedLaboratory"): Dino Dino Jungle has been redesigned to include a laboratory named "Dino Dino Laboratory", with more dinosaurs directly on the course. Besides the dinosaurs, the laboratory doesn't have any other sapient residents in it.
*   [Adaptational Location Change](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdaptationalLocationChange "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdaptationalLocationChange"):
    *   Peach Beach is set at a resort on the shores of _Mario Kart World_'s map instead of in [Isle Delfino](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioSunshine "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioSunshine") like it was in _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDoubleDash "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDoubleDash")_
    *   Choco Mountain is a muddy dirt bike arena manned by Chargin' Chucks instead of a rocky mine set in the mountains like it was in _[Mario Kart 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64")_, although it's located next to an oil refinement facility.
*   [Adaptation Distillation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdaptationDistillation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdaptationDistillation"): Wario Shipyard, a returning course from _[Mario Kart 7](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7")_, features a major redesign to accommodate this game's lack of underwater driving. The track's underwater sections now take place on the water's surface, though they otherwise retain a similar layout.
*   [Adapted Out](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdaptedOut "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdaptedOut"): In previous iterations, Dino Dino Jungle was populated by Noshis, but in _World_, they have been replaced with brachiosaurs and plesiosaurs.
*   [Added Alliterative Appeal](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AddedAlliterativeAppeal "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AddedAlliterativeAppeal"): One of the missions in Free Roam is "Pass by plenty of Pokeys partying on the path!"
*   [Aliens Steal Cattle](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AliensStealCattle "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AliensStealCattle"):
    *   One P-Switch mission has the prompt "SEARCH FIELDS. ABDUCT BLUE COINS.", and puts the player in control of a [Flying Saucer](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FlyingSaucer "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FlyingSaucer") to pick up blue coins with its [Tractor Beam](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TractorBeam "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TractorBeam")... along with, perhaps, the poor Cows who gather around them.
    *   Invoked with the 1.3.0 update, which adds the ability to unlock characters in Free Roam by abducting them with the UFO. The cow, of course, is not exempt from this.
*   [All the Worlds Are a Stage](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllTheWorldsAreAStage "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllTheWorldsAreAStage"): This incarnation of Rainbow Road incorporates elements from several other versions from prior games:
    *   The track itself is one massive lap akin to _[Mario Kart 7](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7")_'s Rainbow Road, while the sheer length of the track also brings to mind the original version of _[Mario Kart 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64")_'s Rainbow Road.
    *   Its first section is a [Level in the Clouds](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LevelInTheClouds "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LevelInTheClouds") above the city like in _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDoubleDash "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDoubleDash")_, which you first access through a cannon, and has a mosaic floor texture akin to _[Super Mario Kart](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart")_'s iteration.
    *   The end of the first section has a split path taking on an 8-like shape, bringing to mind both _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_'s Rainbow Road and the end of _[Mario Kart Wii](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii")_'s Rainbow Road.
    *   The beginning of the second section takes place on a river-like area, bringing to mind the underwater ruins-like nature of Rainbow Downhill in _[Mario Kart Arcade GP](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartArcadeGP "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartArcadeGP")_. The introduction to it also has dash rings in the air, bringing to mind the Glider sections of _[Mario Kart 7](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7")_'s Rainbow Road.
    *   Its third section takes place on a space station like _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_.
    *   The third section has Star Thwomps as hazards like [its SNES incarnation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart"). This segment also has the road in a far more twisted and rotated path, similar to both Anti-Gravity in _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_ and the twisty portions of _[Mario Kart DS](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDS "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDS")_.
    *   The later sections feature a flying train like the _8_\-version of the _[Mario Kart 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64")_ course.
*   [Alliterative Name](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlliterativeName "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlliterativeName"):
    *   Two of the new race tracks introduced in this game are called Salty Salty Speedway and Dandelion Depths.
    *   As per usual, this game introduces its own incarnation of Rainbow Road.
    *   Moo Moo Meadows from _[Mario Kart Wii](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii")_ returns.
    *   Wario's bee costume is called the Wicked Wasp.
*   [Anti-Frustration Features](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AntiFrustrationFeatures "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AntiFrustrationFeatures"):
    *   Items are automatically held behind a racer after getting them in an item box, meaning players no longer have to hold down the trigger if they want to use it as a shield.note 
    *   If a racer has a Bob-omb and another racer crashes into it while it's behind them, it won't also cause the item holder to be caught in the blast.
    *   If you fail a Free Roam mission, you're given the option to instantly retry it by pressing down the Left Stick instead of having to drive back to the starting point. You can also do this if you succeed with the mission, which is useful for when you want to keep looking around the area where the P Switch is located (especially useful when the P Switch was in an area that was hard to reach and return to, as with the three P Switches in the central palace tower of Shy Guy Bazaar).
    *   Upon starting a mission, your character will automatically face the right way so you don't have to reorient yourself to get to the mission's start zone.
    *   When a Star's power is almost up, the jingle from the mainline games now plays to let you know.
    *   The Triple Mushroom item has been reworked. While they still circle around the player, they can no longer be stolen from other players by running into them (Boos and Lightning will still steal/disarm them though). In exchange, running into the circling mushrooms will still give the other player a boost, albeit a smaller one; this in itself is another Anti-Frustration Feature as this can easily happen by mistake in races with 24 players, so the "thief" has less chance of accidentally boosting themselves into a wall or pit.
    *   In contrast to previous games, it is possible to change direction in mid-air (without gliding), giving the player a chance to course-correct if they misalign a jump.
    *   Smart Steering. If the player is about to go off-course, this will automatically and quickly adjust the cart's path rather than making the player do it themselves (sometimes in ways a player can't replicate). If the player prefers not to use this, it can also be turned off in the in-game controller settings. It will also briefly disable itself while boosting items are in use so the player can still use shortcuts.
    *   If the player goes off-road, their vehicle's tires will dramatically inflate into mini monster truck-sizes as a clear indication that you're not on the main path.
    *   Unlike previous titles, where landing in deep off-road hazards like swampy bogs or lava counts as falling off the track, you have a grace period of a few seconds to get out before it's counted as a track fall and Lakitu has to rescue you. This also means that you can use a boost like a Mushroom to take a shortcut across these areas where the danger time doesn't tick down during said boost.
    *   When exiting out of using binoculars, you'll be in the same direction as you were looking before exiting as to help head towards a point of interest you found.
    *   In Single Player and Free Roam modes, the player can press down on the D-Pad to "rewind" their kart's path a set distance, enabling the player to quickly correct a fatal mistake. [With enough skill the rewind can even be used to avoid Spiny Shells](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ExploitedTrope "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ExploitedTrope"), which is quite welcome considering how _Mario Kart_ AI famously takes a mile when given an inch. The catch is that it is _only_ the player that rewinds; the rest of the world and the racers still go forward, and any hazards will still connect (and interrupt the rewind).
    *   Just like in _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_, trophies and stars earned in Grand Prix and Knockout Tour on 100cc or higher will retroactively be added to the lower classes to prevent [Fake Longevity](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FakeLongevity "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FakeLongevity"). Unlike in _8_, this also applies to Mirror Mode.
    *   To easily find characters and their outfits you can sort them by theme and character. NPC Drivers also have their own category which is represented by a Goomba and a Piranha Plant icon.
    *   With Update 1.3.0, unlocking NPC drivers became both possible in Free Roam mode, and much easier to accomplish by hijacking UFOs in the overworld and abducting the character a player wants. Not only does this remove the randomization of the Kamek Orb and provide consistent places to unlock characters, but UFOs work on other players, making it possible for friends to share characters they want with one another. Update 1.4.0's addition of races with custom items makes it possible to spawn _only_ Kamek Orbs from item boxes in a race as well, completely trivializing unlocking the NPC drivers if the player does just a few races on different tracks with only the Orbs enabled.
*   ​["Arabian Nights" Days](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArabianNightsDays "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArabianNightsDays"): Desert Hills and Shy Guy Bazaar, both of which take place in the desert and the latter taking place in a town overlooked by an Middle Eastern palace. Luigi, Daisy and Wario's Oasis costumes also reflects this.
*   [Art Evolution](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtEvolution "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtEvolution"):
    *   The whole game has a livelier, "cartoonier" feel that the developers state is meant to invoke the box art of the original _[Super Mario Kart](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart")_, and which has been compared to _[Super Mario Bros. Wonder](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioBrosWonder "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioBrosWonder")_, though Donkey Kong's design in particular has been altered to match his appearance in _[Donkey Kong Bananza](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/DonkeyKongBananza "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/DonkeyKongBananza")_.

    *   The cars have larger cabins and smaller front and back ends, similar to _[The Super Mario Bros. Movie](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/WesternAnimation/TheSuperMarioBrosMovie "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/WesternAnimation/TheSuperMarioBrosMovie")_.
*   [Artificial Brilliance](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtificialBrilliance "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtificialBrilliance"): Until a later [Nerf](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Nerf "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Nerf") implemented through a patch update, the CPU drivers would use every trick in the book to get ahead, ranging from taking advanced shortcuts, to using Mushrooms to dodge Spiny Shells.

*   [Breaking Old Trends](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BreakingOldTrends "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BreakingOldTrends"):
    *   Tracks from past _Mario Kart_ games are not listed with prefixes (N64, GCN, Wii, etc.) indicating what game they're from. The only other times the series has done this was all the way back in _[Mario Kart DS](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDS "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartDS")_ with its returning battle maps, and _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8") Deluxe_ not using the "Tour" prefix for the non-city tracks added to the Booster Course Pass.
    *   There is no longer a strict divide between "Nitro" cups with new courses and "Retro" cups with returning courses, following the precedent set by _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_'s DLC. The Star and Special Cups (typically Nitro) and the Shell, Banana and Lightning Cups (typically Retro) both feature a mix of old and new courses in this game, while the Flower Cup (typically Nitro) features entirely returning courses and the Leaf Cup (typically Retro) is composed of new courses. For that reason, the Special Cup is the final cup, rather than the Lightning Cup.
    *   In previous entries, every cup has a fully unique set of tracks, and every track is only seen once. Crown City and Peach Stadium break that, with the former appearing in both the Mushroom Cup and Shell Cup, and the latter appearing in both the Shell Cup and the Special Cup. Each cup's icon for the course is different however, and each cup has a different path into and out of the course. These courses each only have one set of time trials, meaning there are only 30 unique courses in this game rather than the standard of 32 set by _DS_.
    *   In previous games, Mario and Luigi had their own circuits, but in this instance the brothers share a track with the appropriate name, "Mario Bros. Circuit". Also, their circuits always took place in [grass areas](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GreenHillZone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GreenHillZone"), but Mario Bros. Circuit evades this by taking place in a [desert area](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StockDesertInterstate "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StockDesertInterstate") instead. This also means this is the first game where Luigi does not have a course exclusive to him (_[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_ originally didn't, but _Deluxe_ added Luigi's Mansion as a battle course).
    *   When a racer is hit with [Lightning](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShockAndAwe "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShockAndAwe"), they play a unique spasming animation instead of the usual spin-out animation.
    *   Only the initial course has you drive multiple laps on the course. The following tracks have you instead drive on a route from the previous track to the next one, with the final lap being on the track itself. Races set on routes begin with a rolling start, another first for the series. However, there is an option to turn off the routes in VS Mode, and Time Trials use the old standard.
    *   Bumping into something is no longer guaranteed to remove all of your momentum; if you clip against a moving object, you may simply be knocked aside while retaining most of your speed. However, a head-on collision still causes a tumble as usual. Additionally, there's a chance that you'll land upside down, sliding on your head for a few seconds before flipping back right-side up. This change also applies to the Bullet Bill item.
    *   Gliders and underwater driving are no longer present after having been a series staple since _[Mario Kart 7](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart7")_, but both have been replaced with new types of driving that hearken back to _[Diddy Kong Racing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/DiddyKongRacing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/DiddyKongRacing")_. In the air, karts sprout wings; when approaching bodies of water, they turn into watercraft. On a related note, the kart-building system introduced in _7_ and featured in subsequent titles has been removed, and players choose from several pre-built karts like in _DS_ and _Wii_.
    *   Drivers can now string together multiple tricks in a single jump to gain even more air time, rather than previous entries limiting you to just one.
    *   Certain large vehicles, like eighteen-wheeler trucks and giant motorboats, are present on some tracks and can be driven into as a temporary power-up, marking the first time in the franchise you can get an ability in a race beyond grabbing an item box or some equivalent.
    *   This is the first installment where you can unlock new drivers mid-race rather than waiting for the player to return to the menu after completing specific conditions. In the case of costumes, those are unlocked by eating a track's special food power-up with a racer you haven't unlocked their costume for yet. Other racers that have historically served as [mooks](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Mook "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Mook") and background characters are unlocked from the player being afflicted with Kamek's curse, which transforms them into a certain character depending on the track.
    *   This is the first game to allow you to explore each track (sans Rainbow Road) at your leisure via Free Roam, whereas in previous titles each track was locked to gameplay modes and players had to use roundabout methods to practice on them like via Time Trial.
    *   This is the first game since _[Mario Kart: Super Circuit](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartSuperCircuit "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartSuperCircuit")_ where Princess Peach in her default dress drives with her hair down, as opposed to wearing a ponytail. She does still sport a ponytail in some of her alternate costumes though.
    *   Coinciding with the addition of costume swaps, this is the first game where the princess-type characters can wear their usual dresses on bikes rather than biker suits, which has been the case since _[Mario Kart Wii](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii")_. Their biker suits can be unlocked as alternate costumes (under the name "Aero").
    *   This is the first mainline game in which Donkey Kong is an unlockable character; he has always been part of the default roster beforehand. This is also the first game where Toadette is a base roster character (discounting _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8") Deluxe_, which had all characters unlocked by default).
    *   Generally the title screen and the selection menus are placed on different screens, but in this game, all of them are merged into one single screen.

*   [Developer's Foresight](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DevelopersForesight "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DevelopersForesight"):
    *   Every track has a road connection to all surrounding tracks. Some of these go unused by Grand Prix and Knockout Tour, but they're fully usable in Versus Race.
    *   It turns out the developers [actually thought about players attempting to follow NPCs to see where they go,![Image 6](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/external_link.gif)](https://youtu.be/6vXdxJA_5sg) and thus NPC behaviour is surprisingly sophisticated for something the vast majority of players will never notice. Drivers will actually go places, park and even get out of their cars rather than just driving in circles (and, rarely, _floor it and drive off the road to take a shortcut_). Pedestrians will enter buildingsnote  (e.g. restaurants). Buses will actually pick up and drop off passengers. Passengers will get off trains when they reach stations. Police cars make a point of patrolling the side roads and backstreets of Crown City when they return from their drives in other areas.
