*   [A Dog Named "Dog"](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ADogNamedDog "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ADogNamedDog"): Among the playable characters are Cow, Dolphin and Penguin.
*   [Drives Like Crazy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DrivesLikeCrazy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DrivesLikeCrazy"): Actively encouraged. In addition to the typical _Mario Kart_ zaniness of boosting and drifting, [grinding on rails](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CarSkiing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CarSkiing") and [riding on walls](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WallJump "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WallJump") have been added to the gameplay mechanics, opening up _a lot_ of potential tricks and shortcuts if you know where to look. A seasoned player tackling Time Trials is going to look like a lunatic behind the wheel.
*   [Easter Egg](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EasterEgg "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EasterEgg"): Akin to _[Mario Kart 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64")_, the [first-place results theme![Image 7](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/external_link.gif)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FZmMadIwi64) has a unique segment that plays after looping several times — in this case, after around five minutes.
*   [Extinct Animal Park](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ExtinctAnimalPark "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ExtinctAnimalPark"): Dino Dino Jungle returns as a retro course, only now it appears to be a park with dinosaurs revived in a laboratory.
*   [Everything Fades](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EverythingFades "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EverythingFades"): Any vehicles that are destroyed by [hijacked trucks](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential") will vanish, alongside their occupants. This also happens to civilians who despawn through a pipe or building.
*   [Fanservice](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Fanservice "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Fanservice"): Peach and Daisy, besides keeping their biker outfits from previous games (now under the "Aero" name), have new outfits that similarly emphasize their figures; Peach has a sightseeing outfit with tight pants, Daisy has a two-piece swimsuit and a [Bedlah Babe](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BedlahBabe "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BedlahBabe") outfit that exposes her midriff, and both of them have touring outfits with short shorts. Rosalina and Pauline also retain their biker suits, though only the former has other outfits.
*   [Feather Fingers](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FeatherFingers "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FeatherFingers"): Since Para-Biddybud is a [Waddling Head](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WaddlingHead "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WaddlingHead") with no hands, it holds up items with its left wing when using them.
*   [Food Porn](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FoodPorn "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FoodPorn"): The Dash Food item comes in dozens of varieties that cater to all kinds of tastes, including [really tall hamburgers](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DagwoodSandwich "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DagwoodSandwich"), sushi boats, pancake stacks, fish and chips, pizzas, ice cream cones, and yogurts.
*   [Forced Transformation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForcedTransformation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForcedTransformation"): Kamek is an item, and when he's called upon, he may use his magic to temporarily transform several racers into a different character. The character chosen depends on the area where he's summoned; an area like Sky-High Sundae turns them into Chargin' Chucks, while an area like Desert Hills turns them into Pokeys. This changes the racer's stats, i.e. kart size and weight, as though they had been selected at the start of the race. Kamek also generally summons a handful of equivalent enemies to serve as obstacles, though this doesn't always occur (for example, Piantas have no equivalent enemy, and Chomps have no equivalent racer). Being transformed into a new character for the first time permanently unlocks them as a selectable racer.
*   [Forest of Perpetual Autumn](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForestOfPerpetualAutumn "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForestOfPerpetualAutumn"): Cheep Cheep Falls and its immediate surroundings are covered in red-leaved _momiji_/maple trees. Meanwhile, the other forests and grasslands in the overworld are as green as ever.
*   [Gentle Giant Sauropod](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GentleGiantSauropod "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GentleGiantSauropod"): _Brachiosaurus_ are among the inhabitants of Dino Dino Jungle. While players can drive along their backs, the sauropods also wander the course and may step on the racers.
*   [Go into the Light](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoIntoTheLight "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoIntoTheLight"): The transition from Peach Stadium to Rainbow Road in the Special Cup has the racers fly upwards into a stream of colorful light surrounded by star-shaped gates. The light eventually covers the entire screen (most likely so the game can unload the world and load in in the [massive track](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MarathonLevel "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MarathonLevel")).
*   [Goofy Feathered Dinosaur](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoofyFeatheredDinosaur "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoofyFeatheredDinosaur"): The _Tyrannosaurus_ are now depicted with feathers on their heads. While fearsome, they look rather goofy due to the game's art style.
*   [Goomba Stomp](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoombaStomp "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoombaStomp"): You can perform tricks by bouncing off obstacles (including Goombas) or even other racers.
*   [Grandfather Clause](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GrandfatherClause "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GrandfatherClause"): The Batadon enemy from _[Super Mario Land](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioLand "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioLand")_ is still called that despite it being a [misreading](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlindIdiotTranslation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlindIdiotTranslation") of its Japanese name Patadon (a combination of the Japanese onomatopoeias for flapping and crushing).
*   [Gravity Screw](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityScrew "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityScrew"): This game's Rainbow Road has this happening during the final two sections. After the racers follow the path from the river to the Glide Ramp that leads to the space station, they find that the station is weirdly oriented to the ground, and as they go through the station, they go upside-down, as though the Anti-Gravity mechanic from _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_ returned (except you can't actually do Spin-Boosts this time and the karts retain their standard gravity physics aside from gravity going in the wrong direction). And come the fourth section, the racers are driving on a road that goes straight down, and not once do they fall off (unless you count driving off the edge of the road)!
*   [Green Gators](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GreenGators "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GreenGators"): The crocodiles in Faraway Oasis are green.
*   [Group Picture Ending](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GroupPictureEnding "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GroupPictureEnding"): The very end of the credits features the main characters of the game — that is, those who can't be summoned by Kamek and have their own costumes — having their picture taken at Mario Bros. Circuit.
*   [Guide Dang It!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GuideDangIt "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GuideDangIt"): The requirements for unlocking Mirror Mode are not hinted at in-game, and are unlikely to be accomplished through regular play. Not only does Mirror Mode require completion of both the Cups and Rallies at 150cc, and finding 10 each of the Free Roam collectibles, but the Special Cup has to be completed _again_ to actually activate the mode; the last task is especially unintuitive since there is little reason to replay a single-player cup after finishing it on the highest speed. However, you can also unlock it if you finish the 150cc Special Cup for the first time after completing the other tasks.
*   [Hailfire Peaks](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HailfirePeaks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HailfirePeaks"): Boo Cinema is a [movie theater](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Studiopolis "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Studiopolis") located in a [gloomy forest](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheLostWoods "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheLostWoods"), playing a [horror movie](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBoosHaunt "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBoosHaunt").
*   [High-Class Gloves](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HighClassGloves "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HighClassGloves"): Besides Peach still having her usual gloves with her main dress, Rosalina's "Aurora" look (returning from Tour) maintains her own.
*   [Humongous Mecha](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HumongousMecha "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HumongousMecha"): A giant robotic Donkey Kong named "Robo DK" patrols DK Spaceport, tossing barrels down slopes. He apperars once more during the final lap of Rainbow Road, riding the train at the end along with several others.
*   [In a Single Bound](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InASingleBound "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InASingleBound"): The Feather item allows you to make a large leap for potential shortcuts. You can also perform a Charge Jump by holding down the drift button while moving straight ahead and releasing it when sparks appear. Though not as powerful as the Feather, this can be used to leap over obstacles, dodge certain incoming attacks, or hop onto rails or walls.
*   [Informed Species](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InformedSpecies "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InformedSpecies"): The ceratopsians roaming around Dino Dino Jungle are identified as _Triceratops_, but they more closely resemble _Nasutoceratops_ in that they have bull-like horns and a flattened nose horn resembling a nasal boss.
*   [Instant Costume Change](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InstantCostumeChange "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InstantCostumeChange"): The new Dash Food item has the effect of changing the characters' appearance, ranging from looking like other powerups across the series to sportswear. Drivers revert to their original outfit at the start of the next race, although the costume is permanently unlocked as a driver in the character select screen. (The "NPC Drivers" cannot change their clothes, however.)
*   [Invisible Anatomy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InvisibleAnatomy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InvisibleAnatomy"): Many of the [newly playable](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PromotedToPlayable "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PromotedToPlayable") species don't have visible limbs to operate their vehicles. Some, like Goomba and Cataquack, have [no arms](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArmlessBiped "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArmlessBiped") to hold the wheel; others, like Peepa and Dolphin, have no legs to reach the pedals; others still, like Pokey and Snowman, have neither arms nor legs.
*   [Invulnerable Civilians](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InvulnerableCivilians "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InvulnerableCivilians"): All non-racer vehicles on the road and NPCs on the street cannot be harmed in by enemy attacks. If a Bomber Bill hits a truck, the Bomber Bill will explode but the truck will take [no damage](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoSell "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoSell"), and attempting to run over a Toad on the streets will lead to you bouncing off them instead. However, you _[can](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential")_ [destroy their vehicles yourself](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential") with a hijacked cargo truck, leading them the vehicle to fly into the air, passengers include, and then [vanish](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EverythingFades "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EverythingFades"), presumably killing everybody inside.
*   [Kicking Ass in All Her Finery](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KickingAssInAllHerFinery "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KickingAssInAllHerFinery"): Much like the previous games, this trope is invoked in a racing style by the four princess-type characters. Unlike Mario Karts Wii and 8, however, they maintain their usual dresses on bikes (and Rosalina also has her "Aurora" look returning from _[Mario Kart Tour](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour")_ letting her consume certain Dash Foods and keep this trope active).
*   [Journey to the Sky](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JourneyToTheSky "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JourneyToTheSky"): Thanks to the game's courses being part of an interconnected overworld and requiring players to head to them on their own in-game via intermission routes, it is now part of the gameplay to take drivers across an upward travel to the courses located in the skies, namely the Great ? Block Ruins and Rainbow Road. The former course makes up for the final destination in Banana Cup and Cloud Rally, and is reached through a very powerful geyser located in the middle of a swampy lake at ground level. Meanwhile, the latter is accessed during Special Cup after driving across Peach Stadium in the third race, and its gateway is a huge, rainbow-colored [Pillar of Light](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PillarOfLight "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PillarOfLight") that drags the drivers upward to the skies (going even higher than the geyser leading to Great ? Block Ruins); in turn, Rainbow Road itself features a key part where drivers ascend even higher, reaching outer space (though the final segment goes back down to complete the extensive loop of the course's layout).
*   [Jurassic Farce](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JurassicFarce "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JurassicFarce"): Dino Dino Jungle has been heavily revamped as a map, now being surrounded by modern-style chain-link fencing and concrete walls, and centring around a facility called the Dino Dino Laboratory, suggesting the dinosaurs having been revived à la _[Jurassic Park](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Franchise/JurassicPark "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Franchise/JurassicPark")_, rather than the track taking place in a [Lost World](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LostWorld "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LostWorld") this time.
*   [Lawyer-Friendly Cameo](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LawyerFriendlyCameo "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LawyerFriendlyCameo"): Yoshi's alternative "Biker" costume resembles [Boshi](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioRPG "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioRPG"), being a blue Yoshi in leather punk gear, but it's not quite an exact match to skirt around any legal issues surrounding Boshi's character, as he is co-owned by [Square Enix](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/SquareEnix "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/SquareEnix").
*   [Leaning on the Fourth Wall](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LeaningOnTheFourthWall "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LeaningOnTheFourthWall"): The end credits display a newspaper story about Rainbow Road making an unexpected return. While it's most explicitly about how Rainbow Road gets magically conjured into the game world after completing all the other Grand Prix cups, it also references how _Mario Kart World_ is the first new _Mario Kart_ game in a long time and how this is the first new version of Rainbow Road since _[Mario Kart 8](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart8")_ in 2014 (the _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ DLC and _[Mario Kart Tour](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour")_ released in the meantime instead featured [Nostalgia Level](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NostalgiaLevel "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NostalgiaLevel") takes on previous Rainbow Road iterations).
*   [Legendary Carp](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LegendaryCarp "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LegendaryCarp"): [Cheep Cheep Falls](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Wutai "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Wutai") features as a minor stage hazard Cheep Cheeps swimming against the current of a waterfall, which is a _Mario_ spin on the Japanese myth about koi becoming dragons by climbing waterfalls.
*   [Level Ate](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LevelAte "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LevelAte"):
    *   The returning track Sky-High Sundae is a gigantic resort made out of ice cream and other frozen treats, which is run by Toadette considering it's got her name branding over them. The credits also have a newspaper article noting that the nature of the resort purely selling sweets [resulted in a rise of dentist cases](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SurprisinglyRealisticOutcome "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SurprisinglyRealisticOutcome").
    *   ​Downplayed with Choco Mountain. The course itself is a massive oil drill with elements of a monster truck arena, with the oil actually being liquid chocolate. It is still a step up from the course's prior appearances in the series, where it was strictly a [Death Mountain](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DeathMountain "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DeathMountain") location and its name only alluded to an [Edible Theme Naming](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EdibleThemeNaming "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EdibleThemeNaming") inherited from the courses of _[Super Mario Kart](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart")_ (which in turn carried over the theme naming of the levels from _[Super Mario World](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioWorld "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioWorld")_).
*   [Level in Reverse](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LevelInReverse "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LevelInReverse"): Like in most cups from _[Mario Kart Tour](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartTour")_, certain courses in VS and Knockout Tour modes are traversed in reverse. Mirror Mode, a series staple, also returns and can even be accessed in Free Roam after it's unlocked for other modes by going to the castle at Peach Stadium and going through the big stained glass window of Princess Peach in the central tower.
*   [Long Song, Short Scene](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LongSongShortScene "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LongSongShortScene"): Each segment of Rainbow Road (including the route from Peach Stadium) has its own theme that plays until you reach the next segment, but if you are racing at 150cc, you are only likely to hear the entirety of the final section's theme. The course can be completed in under five minutes, but the complete themes for each segment add to a little over eight minutes of music without looping.
*   [Macro Zone](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MacroZone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MacroZone"): "Acorn Heights" takes place around a supersized oak, where the racers drive across and beneath giant grass leaves, platform off of mushrooms, and dodge gigantic rolling acorns.
*   [Marathon Level](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MarathonLevel "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MarathonLevel"):
    *   Each Knockout Tour rally consists of a nonstop transcontinental race across six select tracks. Each track in turn serves as a checkpoint, with the last four racers per checkpoint below the threshold eliminated until only four remain.
    *   This game's incarnation of Rainbow Road is easily the longest individual track in franchise history, with elite Time Trial players recording times exceeding **four minutes**, and likely to take over five minutes to finish in a standard race. Unlike _[Mario Kart 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64")_'s versions of Wario Stadium and Rainbow Road, it's broken up into segments instead of consisting of multiple laps (four, to be exact, five if you count the transition from Peach's Stadium). By extension, this also gives Special Cup the distinction of being the longest cup in the game _and_ the series, as it also has the lengthy Mario Circuit (a combination of the first three SNES Mario Circuits) and what's by far the most prolonged intermission route in Grand Prix (namely between the aforementioned Mario Circuit and Peach Stadium, including a pass through Moo Moo Meadows from Lightning Cup).
*   [Mêlée à Trois](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MeleeATrois "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MeleeATrois"): For the first time in the series, more than just two teams can be pit against each other in Battle Mode and Vs Race, with a maximum of four teams.
*   [Mining for Cookies](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MiningForCookies "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MiningForCookies"): Choco Mountain has been heavily industrialized with oil pumps and mineshafts, with the twist that the workers are digging for veins of chocolate syrup.
*   [Misplaced Wildlife](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MisplacedWildlife "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MisplacedWildlife"): Bison are among the inhabitants of Faraway Oasis, despite the map being based on African plains and having otherwise appropriate fauna such as giraffes and elephants.
*   [Mistaken for Granite](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MistakenForGranite "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MistakenForGranite"): The moai-like Tokotokos and Batadons on Desert Hills will start off mostly dormant before waking up on later laps and moving around the course.
*   [Monstrous Scenery](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MonstrousScenery "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MonstrousScenery"):
    *   In the Boo Cinema course, crowds of Boos and a few giant Boohemoths leer at and taunt the racers from the course edges.
    *   In the Spiny Rally, in the transition between Peach Beach and Wario's Shipyard, a huge Dragoneel can be seen arching in and out of the water beyond the track's boundaries.
*   [Musical Nod](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MusicalNod "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MusicalNod"):
    *   In Free Roam and when racing between courses in Grand Prix and VS Race, arrangements of many tunes throughout the _Mario_ franchise can be heard, ranging from songs for _Mario Kart_ courses that are otherwise absent from _World_, to songs from mainline platformers such as "Dire, Dire Docks" from _[Super Mario 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMario64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMario64")_ and "Space Junk Road" from _[Super Mario Galaxy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioGalaxy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioGalaxy")_, to even other spin-offs such as _[Mario Paint](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioPaint "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioPaint")_ and the _[Yoshi's Island](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/YoshisIsland "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/YoshisIsland")_ and _[Wario](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/Wario "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/Wario")_ franchises, all the way to "The Mario Drawing Song" from _Flipnote Studio_.
    *   The music that plays throughout DK Spaceport is a jazz arrangement of the 25m theme from the original _[Donkey Kong](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/DonkeyKong1981 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/DonkeyKong1981")_ arcade game. Moreover, the music that plays during the final section of the course is an arrangement of the Hammer theme from the same game.
    *   The music that plays in Starview Peak includes parts of "Rosalina in the Observatory" from _[Super Mario Galaxy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioGalaxy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioGalaxy")_ in its melody.
    *   The music that plays during the final section of Rainbow Road includes a brief quote of the staff credits theme from _[Super Mario Kart](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/SuperMarioKart")_.
*   [Mythology Gag](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MythologyGag "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MythologyGag"):
    *   One of the businesses seen in a city track is a [Koopa Hotel](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/HotelMario "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/HotelMario").
    *   The primary karts for Mario, Peach, and Toad in the trailers are the standard kart, a bike, and the [Tiny Titan](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii"), bringing to mind the vehicles they choose in _[The Super Mario Bros. Movie](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/WesternAnimation/TheSuperMarioBrosMovie "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/WesternAnimation/TheSuperMarioBrosMovie")_. Meanwhile, the Super Star item now has an iridescent jewel-like texture to it similar to its depiction in the movie.
    *   A sign in Moo Moo Meadows notes the farm was established in 2008, referring to the year _[Mario Kart Wii](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKartWii")_, where the track originated, was released.
*   [Nerf](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Nerf "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Nerf"): A number of offensive items have had their effects lessened, likely to account for the fact there are now double the number of racers as before, so the likelihood of being struck by another racer is much greater (as is the scenario of being stun-locked by being struck by several items in rapid succession).
    *   The Bullet Bill item is much slower than in previous games, where it was the fastest way to travel, and can now be outrun by mushroom boosts. Combined with the far larger tracks to evade them their effectiveness is much lower. In addition, colliding with another racer in this state no longer guarantees a tumble, instead having a similar effect to bumping into a moving vehicle. Also, you can no longer use it to take most shortcuts because it will just backtrack and rejoin the road.
    *   The duration a racer is flattened by a Mega Mushroom user is significantly shorter, almost lasting two seconds before returning to normal. Additionally, it now stays in the item slot until it wears off, so waiting until the next item box set before using it isn't a viable strategy anymore.
    *   The Lightning item no longer shrinks all opponents, instead only shrinking the players ahead of the user. In addition, the duration of the shrinking has been drastically reduced.
    *   The Fire Flower's ammo has been reduced from 10 to 8 fireballs.
    *   Due to tumbling being physics-based now, getting hit by a shell or banana is not nearly as punishing; rather than spinning in place and losing all momentum, you're likely to fall forward when struck and not lose so much distance.
    *   While you still get a speed boost for bumping into the Triple Mushroom of another racer, you can no longer steal them and the speed boost you get is smaller than from using your own Mushroom.
    *   In Patch 1.2.0, CPU drivers in games other than Battle Mode were made weaker.
    *   The speed boost you get from coins has been heavily nerfed and being maxed out now only adds 5% to your top speed.

*   [Video Game Cruelty Potential](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VideoGameCrueltyPotential"):
    *   You can destroy certain objects in Free Roam mode, such as benches, tablets, and camping equipment. Ironically, civilians not only won't mind you doing this, but will _[cheer](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SkewedPriorities "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SkewedPriorities")_ the player occasionally, even though you just ruined their camping trip.
    *   The cargo trucks. You can control one as long as it has red neon signs on the sides of it by entering from behind. _Any_ vehicle you run into will be tossed aside. But unlike with invinciblity from a Super Star, the vehicles will _vanish_, strongly indicating you killed anyone in it. You can easily kill dozens of people with one truck before it explodes on it's own, with _[nobody](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KarmaHoudini "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KarmaHoudini")_ [caring one bit](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KarmaHoudini "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KarmaHoudini"), [not even the police](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PoliceAreUseless "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PoliceAreUseless").
*   [Wall Jump](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WallJump "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WallJump"): One of the new mechanics allow drivers to ride and bounce off of certain walls.
*   [Wicked Wasps](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WickedWasps "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WickedWasps"): One of [Wario](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EvilCounterpart "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EvilCounterpart")'s outfits gives him a wasp suit, which is even called Wicked Wasp.
*   [Wide-Open Sandbox](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WideOpenSandbox "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WideOpenSandbox"): All tracks exist in an open world. The Grand Prix mode sees players traveling from course-to-course while a Free Roam mode allows you to drive around the entire map.
*   [Written Sound Effect](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WrittenSoundEffect "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WrittenSoundEffect"): Various item effects now cause written sound effects in the vein of _[Mario Kart 64](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64 "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/VideoGame/MarioKart64")_, such as "BOOOM" for Bob-omb explosions, "KABOOOM" for Spiny Shell explosions, and "BEEEP" for Super Horn honks. In Mirror Mode, they're drawn backwards like several other elements.
*   [Wutai](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Wutai "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Wutai"): Cheep Cheep Falls take place in an area filled with Japanese pagodas.
*   [Your Size May Vary](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/YourSizeMayVary "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/YourSizeMayVary"):
    *   The Cow playable as a racer is roughly the same size as Mario and the others. The non-playable cows on Moo Moo Meadows, in contrast, are about three times as big as a kart.
    *   In general, the characters and buildings in the world are scaled much larger relative to the size of the kart drivers. Yoshi, Shy Guy, and Toad NPCs are all at least twice as big as the Yoshi, Shy Guy, and Toad drivers, while Peach's Castle is now humongous.
*   [Zip Mode](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ZipMode "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ZipMode"): In Free Roam, going to the map allows you to pick one track to go to automatically. You can also select one of the other characters on the map to begin playing as them from their current position.

| | **Moo Moo Meadows** is the second race course of the [Mushroom Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_Cup "Mushroom Cup") in _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_. The course is inspired by and serves as a successor to the _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_ track [Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm"). An arrangement of Moo Moo Meadows' music is heard in the second half of the credits music along with [Luigi Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Luigi_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_Wii/) "Luigi Circuit (Mario Kart Wii)")/[Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_Wii/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart Wii)") and [Maple Treeway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Maple_Treeway "Maple Treeway"). The course returns as a [classic course](https://www.mariowiki.com/Classic_course "Classic course") in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ where it is the first course of the [Shell Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shell_Cup "Shell Cup"), and in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_ as the first course of the [Lightning Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning_Cup "Lightning Cup"). In both _World_ and the original version of _8_, it is also used in [Battle Mode](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle_Mode "Battle Mode"). Battle Mode in _8_ does not change Moo Moo Meadows' layout at all, while in _World_ multiple pathways are opened up in the middle. In _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, a similar course known as [Windmill Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Windmill_Meadows "Windmill Meadows"), which reuses the _Mario Kart 8_ version of its music, was added in the version 2.0.0 update. _Mario Kart Wii_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Mario Kart Wii")\] -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ### Course layout\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Course layout")\] [![Image 25: Wii Moo Moo Meadows from Mario Kart Wii](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/88/MKWii-MooMooMeadows2.png/200px-MKWii-MooMooMeadows2.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWii-MooMooMeadows2.png) The course is located in a rural area of green hills, with a river near a farm, and a few trees surrounding the track. The scenery around the track includes a milk cart, a barn, a windmill, a river with a bridge and some dirty paths leading to outside the meadows. At the start of the track, there is a brief straightaway and then a gradual turn left, passing a farm with a silo. About halfway through this turn is the first set of [Item Boxes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Item_Box "Item Box"). Then, there is another turn to the left leading the racer into the meadows where several [Moo Moos](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") are grazing. On the first lap, they stay to the side of the road, but on the other laps, the Moo Moos cross the road, serving as obstacles for the players. If one happens to run into a Moo Moo, they flip over and lose their item. There are two herds of Moo Moos - one in the middle area of the meadow, and the other one in the turn exiting it. After racers serpentine through the meadow, they encounter the second item set followed by a slight right turn and a simple blue ramp. After the ramp, there is a left turn where racers will encounter the first of several [Monty Moles](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole"). The Monty Moles will burrow around the track, leaving behind dirt trails that slow racers down, before stopping and trying to pop out of the ground to hit racers. After the left turn, racers enter an open area with multiple routes; several small grassy hills lie throughout the track and racers must weave around them, though there is a [dash panel](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Panel "Dash Panel") ramp that allows them to jump over the first hill. The last item set can be found here; there are Item Boxes both floating in midair above the hill, and to the left and right of the hill. Several more Monty Moles are also found around the hills. After this section, there is a slight left turn and racers then reach the finish line. Moo Moo Meadows is one of two courses in _Mario Kart Wii_, along with [SNES Ghost Valley 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ghost_Valley_2 "Ghost Valley 2"), that did not have an online tournament take place on it. ### Shortcuts\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Shortcuts")\] The first notable set of shortcuts can be found in the meadow. Two of the turns can be cut off, each only requiring a single [Mushroom](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Mushroom "Dash Mushroom"), but if the player has other speed items they can cross the entire meadow without needing to stay on the road. This can be especially beneficial when the Moo Moos are crossing the road itself. The second notable set of shortcuts can be found in the final section with the grassy hills; the player can use speed items to drive over the hills to save time and avoid being slowed down by the Monty Moles. _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Mario Kart 8 / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")\] -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- [![Image 26: Wii Moo Moo Meadows in Mario Kart 8](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/8f/MK8_Wii_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png/250px-MK8_Wii_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MK8_Wii_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png) Wii Moo Moo Meadows in _Mario Kart 8_ Moo Moo Meadows makes its classic course debut in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ as the first course of the [Shell Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shell_Cup "Shell Cup"). The course is also available in the [Battle Mode](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle_Mode "Battle Mode") of the Wii U version of _Mario Kart 8_. Its layout is mostly retained but has several notable changes. The track as a whole is more varied and uneven in elevation. At the turn after the simple ramp, the outside of the turn has been elevated and ends in a [glide ramp](https://www.mariowiki.com/Glide_Ramp "Glide Ramp"). The hills at the ending section have also significantly been reduced in size, expanding the main track as a result. The Monty Moles no longer leave behind trails that slow down racers; instead, the trails can be used as ramps for racers to perform [tricks](https://www.mariowiki.com/Jump_Boost "Jump Boost") off of. Lastly, the first set of Item Boxes now appears at the start of the first turn, the last item set is removed altogether, and Double Item Boxes appear at the second item set in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_. The course also has received several visual and auditory changes. The time of day has changed to morning, and a rooster can be heard crowing at the start of the course intro. There are now more farms, variations of Moo Moos, and windmills. The once-bobbing trees are now stationary trees. The start/finish line banner is now similar to the banner on [Thwomp Ruins](https://www.mariowiki.com/Thwomp_Ruins "Thwomp Ruins") and uses the modern _Mario Kart_ logo. The music is now orchestrated, using more fiddle in the theme. Based on a city map that can be found in [Super Bell Subway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Bell_Subway "Super Bell Subway"), Moo Moo Meadows is shown to be located on the outskirts area of the city that contains both [Toad Harbor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad_Harbor "Toad Harbor") and [Wii Wario's Gold Mine](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario%27s_Gold_Mine "Wario's Gold Mine"), as well as the same city that [N64 Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Mario_Kart_64/) "Rainbow Road (Mario Kart 64)") hovers over.[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows#cite_note-1) _Mario Kart World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Mario Kart World")\] ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ [![Image 27: Moo Moo Meadows in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/3/3c/MKWorldMooMooMeadows.png/200px-MKWorldMooMooMeadows.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorldMooMooMeadows.png) Moo Moo Meadows in _Mario Kart World_ Moo Moo Meadows returns in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_, appearing as the first course of the [Lightning Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning_Cup "Lightning Cup"). This makes it the first course in the series' history to appear as a classic course twice in a row in the base game, as [SNES Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Super_Mario_Kart/) "Rainbow Road (Super Mario Kart)"), [Wii Coconut Mall](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coconut_Mall "Coconut Mall"), [N64 Kalimari Desert](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kalimari_Desert "Kalimari Desert"), [DS Waluigi Pinball](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi_Pinball_/(race_course/) "Waluigi Pinball (race course)"), [Wii Mushroom Gorge](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_Gorge "Mushroom Gorge"), [Wii Maple Treeway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Maple_Treeway "Maple Treeway"), [Wii Koopa Cape](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Cape "Koopa Cape"), and [GCN Daisy Cruiser](https://www.mariowiki.com/Daisy_Cruiser_/(race_course/) "Daisy Cruiser (race course)") were all in _Mario Kart 7_ but were DLC courses in their _Mario Kart 8_ reappearance. The course also appears as the third checkpoint of the [Golden Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Golden_Rally "Golden Rally"), the second checkpoint of the [Moon Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moon_Rally "Moon Rally"), and the fourth checkpoint of the [Heart Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Heart_Rally "Heart Rally"). It is the first Mushroom Cup course to appear as a classic course in the Lightning Cup, and one of two overall alongside [Toad's Factory](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Factory "Toad's Factory"). A barn with a giant statue of a [cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") driving a motorcycle has been added in the center of the course. [Kamek](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kamek_/(item/) "Kamek (item)") will turn racers into either [Cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") or [Para-Biddybud](https://www.mariowiki.com/Para-Biddybud "Para-Biddybud"). The course is also passed through in the [Special Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Special_Cup "Special Cup") between [Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart World)") and [Peach Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Stadium "Peach Stadium"), making it one of the few courses to directly be part of a route between two other courses (another is [Koopa Troopa Beach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Troopa_Beach_/(Super_Mario_Kart/) "Koopa Troopa Beach (Super Mario Kart)"), which is part of the route between [DK Spaceport](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Spaceport "DK Spaceport") and Peach Stadium). The course is very similar to its iteration from _Mario Kart 8_. A few more cows serve as obstacles, the track contains a few more hills outside of the grassy hills, and a shortcut ramp on the left-hand side replaces the ramp over the grassy hills. The music appears to be a hybrid of the _Mario Kart Wii_ and _Mario Kart 8_ arrangements, combining the emphasized beat of the former with the melody of the latter. Geographically, the course is located in the center of the map, in the middle of the grassy plains region. There is a sign stating that the farm has been in activity since 2008, referencing _Mario Kart Wii_'s release date. ### Battle\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Battle")\] The track also appears as a battle course, though unlike in the original _Mario Kart 8_, various routes have been added within the center of the track to make it a more traditional battle experience.[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows#cite_note-2) The paths that are opened up primarily lead to the barn with the Cow statue, which is also opened up. An arrangement of the theme for [Chain Chomp Wheel](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chain_Chomp_Wheel "Chain Chomp Wheel") from _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_ plays on this version of the course. ### Routes\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=7 "Edit section: Routes")\] There are four distinct paths that enter Moo Moo Meadows, depending on the route taken to reach the course. * Traveling from [Crown City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Crown_City "Crown City"), [Choco Mountain](https://www.mariowiki.com/Choco_Mountain "Choco Mountain"), or [Toad's Factory](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Factory "Toad's Factory") enters the course from the final turn, behind the starting line. * Traveling from [DK Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Pass "DK Pass"), [Dandelion Depths](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dandelion_Depths "Dandelion Depths"), [Dry Bones Burnout](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dry_Bones_Burnout "Dry Bones Burnout"), or [Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart World)") enters the course from the top, travelling through the barn in the center of the track before turning to the left through the starting line. * Traveling from [Cheep Cheep Falls](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cheep_Cheep_Falls_/(race_course/) "Cheep Cheep Falls (race course)") enters the course from the first turn, traveling to the starting line to traverse the course in reverse. * Traveling from [Peach Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Stadium "Peach Stadium") enters the course from just in front of the starting line, turning left to traverse the course in reverse. * [![Image 28: From Crown City](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/0/02/Crown_City_-_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png/20px-Crown_City_-_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Crown_City_-_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png "From Crown Moo Moo Meadows appears in _[Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_%26_Sonic_at_the_London_2012_Olympic_Games_/(Wii/) "Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games (Wii)")_ as the location of the [Dream Equestrian](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dream_Equestrian "Dream Equestrian") event, though the event uses a track with a completely different layout. Players must travel through the track carrying a wagon full of seven [Yoshi eggs](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi_Egg "Yoshi Egg") and reach the finish line. The course features [Kamek](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kamek "Kamek"), who tries to throws obstacles in the players' path, and a [Chain Chomp](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chain_Chomp "Chain Chomp") that appears before the conclusion of the event. A badge mentions Moo Moo Meadows directly in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_. The badge depicts a logo for Moo Moo Meadows Milk, and was added in the [2023 Mii Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii_Tour_/(2023/) "Mii Tour (2023)"). The Moo Moo Meadows logo also appears in [GCN Waluigi Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi_Stadium_/(Mario_Kart:_Double_Dash!!/) "Waluigi Stadium (Mario Kart: Double Dash!!)"). 05/21/25[Learn more](https://www.nintendo.com/en-ca/store/products/mario-kart-world-switch-2/)

Ask the Developer Vol. 18: Mario Kart World — Part 3
----------------------------------------------------

*   This article has been translated from the original Japanese content.
    
*   This interview was conducted before the game was released.
    

In this 18th volume of Ask the Developer, an interview series in which developers convey in their own words Nintendo's thoughts about creating products and the unusual details they hone in on, we're talking to the developers behind the [_Mario Kart™ World_](https://www.nintendo.com/en-ca/store/products/mario-kart-world-switch-2/) game, a [Nintendo Switch™ 2](https://www.nintendo.com/en-ca/gaming-systems/switch-2/features/) game that launches alongside the Nintendo Switch 2 system on Thursday, June 5.

  
Check out the rest of the interview
--------------------------------------

**  
Part 3: An interconnected world**
--------------------------------------

**You mentioned that the amount of content ended up increasing. You also drew a lot of concept art for this game.**

**Ishikawa:** The designers came up with various ideas, thinking that if the theme was a vast world, they could show things other than racing. There were sketches of characters, scenery, costumes that matched the various landscapes, characters eating... We had a vast, interconnected world in mind, so a good deal of the concept art depicted scenes of people’s lives there. We designed the costumes and vehicles as a set and created these poster-style designs.

![Image 1](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_10)

**Oh, even though it's** **_Mario Kart_****, there are some that show the characters eating food instead of driving a kart.**

**Yabuki:** The idea of showing characters eating a variety of foods came up early on in development.

**Jikumaru:** If you're traveling through a vast and diverse world, you can’t leave out the local food that's unique to each place. But actually, we did consider removing the food feature at one point. Incorporating it into the game means adding not only the food itself, but also the stores that sell it and the staff that work there, which would mean even more content.

**But you came back to this idea later?**

**Jikumaru:** Yes, while development was ongoing, about two years after the idea came up, I thought to myself, “You know what? I need food!” (Laughs) Unable to let it go, I asked the programmers to implement a hamburger model I'd created and make it so that the characters could eat it. It was well received within the team, and the designer started to churn out different kinds of food. Before we knew it, the number of variations had exploded.

**Ishikawa:** The designer in charge was really pumped up about creating them. We've incorporated lots of Mario-inspired twists and tidbits to create a wide variety of designs. I also had a lot of fun looking at those designs.

![Image 2](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_11)

**Sato**: Food is sold at “Yoshi's,” fictional drive-thru restaurants located all over the game's world. Yoshi and his friends make food inspired by each area.

**So, “Yoshi's” is a chain of drive-thrus that's expanded across the world.**

**Ishikawa**: Exactly. For example, a Yoshi's drive-thru located in a volcanic region would look like a volcano and sell piping-hot soup inspired by Bowser. (Laughs)

**Jikumaru**: As we were making these various concepts, Yabuki-san comes marching up to me and says, “When Mario eats something, he transforms.” He sounded pretty serious about it. (Laughs)

**Yabuki**: Originally, we were creating the various outfits separately from the foods. So, we wondered if we could combine those two elements.

**Oh, so the foods and outfits were unrelated at first?**

**Yabuki**: Yes, they were two completely separate elements. We discussed the idea of using coins to buy clothes from clothing stores, but that would have meant stopping at stores to shop, which would have disrupted the flow, given that this is a world where you can keep driving. That's when the idea of food came up. We thought, why don’t we have a drive-thru system where characters eat while driving, and eating makes them change outfits or transform into a different character? Though, it's utterly ridiculous. (Laughs)

**But in the world of Mario, it probably doesn't feel so strange.**

**Yabuki**: Then, the question came up: “Does Mario, in fact, eat mushrooms?” (Laughs)

**Jikumaru:** So in the midst of development, we went up to Tezuka-san (8) and asked him to confirm, “Is Mario actually eating those mushrooms?”

**(8)** _Takashi Tezuka. Executive Officer and Producer of the Planning & Development Division. Primarily involved in the development of 2D Mario games in the Super Mario Bros. series. Previously appeared in_ [_Ask the Developer Vol. 11, Super Mario Bros. Wonder._](https://www.nintendo.com/en-ca/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-11-super-mario-bros-wonder-part-1/)

**Yabuki**: That's right. And Tezuka-san answers, “Yeah, he is.”

**Everyone**: (Laughs)

**Jikumaru**: Plus, the idea of eating food from a particular region and then changing into an outfit associated with that region fits the game perfectly. As you're racing, it's a real delight to see players changing one by one into the local outfit for that area.

**Yabuki**: Not all characters have outfits that change by eating food, but some have a variety that you can pick up while driving around and eating, so we hope this will be a good incentive for players to try out different characters.

**Now that you mention it, some of the new characters in this game seem like unlikely picks. I was surprised to see Cow as one of the playable characters.**

**Yabuki**: That's right. In previous games in the series, Cow was part of the scenery or an obstacle on one of the courses. But when we were working on an early version of a course in this game set on a ranch that players can drive through, this sketch came up. (Laughs)

![Image 3](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_12_updated)

**Oh, I thought Cow was just on the back of the truck, but she's actually driving it. (Laughs)**

**Ishikawa**: Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that's when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.

![Image 4](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_13)

The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn't feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world.

**Sato**: We called these types of characters “NPC drivers.” In other words, non-player character drivers.

**Yabuki**: So it was like, “They're NPCs, but they're playable? Which is it?” (Laughs) It's pretty funny to see a four-legged Cow holding onto motorcycle handlebars with her front hooves.

**Ishikawa**: But when she jumps, she strikes a proper quadrupedal pose. So I'm pretty sure Cow is still in touch with her animal nature. (Laughs)

**Jikumaru**: It was thanks to the introduction of various “NPC drivers” that the idea to have Kamek appear as an item was born. When Kamek casts a spell, the racers are transformed into playable NPCs, so one by one they might all turn into Cow mid-race. I think it turned out to be a unique item that has never been seen before. In fact, Cow is a character who's inspired a lot of different ideas, including obstacle characters like Camel and Giraffe.

**Ishikawa**: Cow is actually a pivotal character in the _Mario Kart_ series. (Laughs)

**Asahi**: On the other hand, when previously non-playable characters like Cow become playable, it means giving them new ways to express emotion, which must have been difficult for the voice lead. We were conscious of depicting the personalities and characteristics of “NPC drivers” in a way that doesn't look inferior to classic characters like Mario. The voice team members went through a lot of trial and error in the pursuit of the ideal sound. In addition to more characters, this game also has a wider selection of vehicles for characters to drive, so it was a huge task to create engine sounds that matched the characteristics, such as the appearance and structure, of each vehicle. We tried out a lot of different sounds in our search for something ideal—we even used croaking frogs and beating drums. (Laughs)

**Sato**: There are a lot of vehicles in this game, too. Since the game is about racing around the world, we've included not only race karts, but also everyday vehicles. It must have been tough for the designers, as they had to not only design the body of the vehicle, but also consider how the tires would transform when drifting and how the vehicle would move when jumping.

**I see. Because players are driving in a vast, interconnected world, you designed vehicles that can handle a variety of driving styles and circumstances.**

**Ishikawa**: That's right. For example, the Standard Kart has a higher ride height in this game, and suspension movement has been added so that when you drive it, the tires move in accordance with the unevenness of the surface and your actions.

Since players are driving in a vast world, we wanted them to enjoy racing not only on asphalt, like on a racetrack, but also on rough, off-road surfaces. This was made possible thanks to the programmers' careful attention to the vehicle movements. We also wanted it to be fun to choose a vehicle based on the world's different locations and situations, so we tried to make the lineup as varied and distinct as possible.

**In terms of the design, in the previous game,** **_Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_****, you drove underwater, but in this game, you can drive on water, right?**

![Image 5](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Pop_Up/Popup_06)

**Sato**: Yes. Since you drive on water, we put a lot of effort into the wave graphics, too. Not just how they look—our up-and-coming programmers also implemented simulations, such as ripples spreading when something drops in the water, or waves appearing after a vehicle passes through. They made it possible to create waves on demand. This game has enemy characters that create waves when they attack, so we were able to incorporate players jumping on those waves into the gameplay.

**Jikumaru**: Racing on water is something this game has in common with the _Wave Race 64_™ (9) game.

**(9)** _Nintendo 64 software released in November 1996 in North America. Players race across the water on watercrafts at full throttle, competing for time and technique._

**Ishikawa**: That's right—when it came to the jumping action, Jikumaru-san, you were very particular about the whitecaps of the waves, right?

**Jikumaru**: Ah, you noticed that. (Laughs) If you want an exhilarating jump on a wave, you need to be able to see the crest of the wave to gauge the timing of your jump. But with regular wave visuals, it's hard to tell where the crest of the wave is. That's why I asked for white foam, or whitecaps, to be added to the crests. I was like, “Hmm, I don't see any whitecaps on the waves...” Then the programmers would say, “How about now, Jikumaru-san?” And I'd be like, “I still can't see it! Just a little more!” We went back and forth like this for a while before the job was done. The programmers really worked hard. Thanks to that, I think jumping on waves has turned into a nice little gameplay element.

![Image 6](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_14)

**Was that also part of your commitment to user-friendliness?**

**Jikumaru**: Yes. But while we continued to work on this, the designers started to request different ways to express water, not just from a gameplay perspective, but also in terms of the visual portrayal of beaches and shoals.

**Ishikawa**: I wanted to show the shoal floor through the crystal-clear water. At first, we were worried that we wouldn't be able to show the shoal floor because it was demanding on the processor. But our programmers made improvements here and there, and we were able to make it happen. Even with the familiar Koopa Troopa Beach course, we were able to create the visuals we wanted to show... Thank you for that, Sato-san.

**Sato**: Because we were so particular about this, the designers needed to toil away to make the shoal floor visible. (Laughs) But thanks to their efforts, it improved the quality of the graphics.

**Ishikawa**: You must’ve also worked hard to create the sound you hear when driving on water, right, Asahi-san?

**Asahi**: That’s right. Unlike driving on land, when driving on water, the vehicle bobs up and down along with the movement of the water. The sound is designed to correspond to the vehicle's movement and orientation. It was created with great attention paid to even the most delicate sounds, so please listen out for it when you're driving on water.

Charmed by the introduction of a cow racer for the new Mario Kart World game, fans have made her the focus of videos that are surfacing in people’s Instagram and TikTok feeds.

![Image 1: An image from the Mario Kart World video game shows a smiling cow with a nose ring riding a purple motorcycle.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2025/06/25/multimedia/00xp-mario-cow/00xp-mario-cow-articleLarge.png?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)

The decision to elevate the cow, previously a background figure, into a playable character for the new Mario Kart World game has proved to be a popular one among Nintendo fans.Credit...Nintendo

July 13, 2025

Think of the name Nintendo, and familiar names and faces likely come to mind. There’s Mario and Luigi, the mustachioed brothers in overalls who fight Bowser, the turtlelike villain with a habit of kidnapping Princess Peach. And then there’s Donkey Kong, Wario and Toad, among others.

These characters have been racing one another in iterations of the Mario Kart game series since 1992, with no real story line other than who can come in first place. But from the moment the [first trailers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pE23YTYEZM) for the Switch 2 console and the Mario Kart World game were released in April, fans were abuzz that a new favorite had entered the race: a cow.

Fascination with Cow, as the character is known, only grew after the console and game went on sale last month. She has become Mario Kart World’s breakout star, validated by her leading role in popular videos on Instagram and TikTok.

One Instagram reel, featuring the cow rocking back and forth on a go-kart [to the beat of “Mooo!”](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DKnFz9-xwij/?igsh=MWprdnJ3NDA1cDB3Zg%3D%3D) by Doja Cat, has been viewed 1.9 million times. Another has her [showboating on a motorcycle](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DLGRJgTRQSm/?igsh=MXhxMDNlbTU5YzExaA%3D%3D) to “La Vaca” (“The Cow”), the 2000 merengue hit by Mala Fe.

Both videos are the creation of Jorge Martinez of McAllen, Texas, who said he was excited about the cow from the moment he first saw the trailer for the game.

_“_Oh, I lost it,” he said. “I wasn’t even thinking about memes. I was just thinking about playing as a cow_.”_

[**Mario Kart World**](https://www.ign.com/wikis/mario-kart-world) features the biggest roster of racer Characters yet, dwarfing the sizes of all previous Mario Kart games, thanks to the inclusion of not just the main Mario cast, but also several creatures found across all of the Super Mario games!

There are also several types of unique costumes and outfits for each of the main Racer Characters in MKW, further adding variety and style to the racers you can choose from. The number of costumes ranges from two to 10, including that character's default outfit.

This guide teaches you how to unlock Characters and their outfits in Mario Kart World, and lists every costume for each Character, along with checkmarks to track your exact progress toward unlocking them all.

How to Unlock Outfits in Mario Kart World
-----------------------------------------

Outfits and costumes in Mario Kart World are permanently unlocked by picking up Food Powerups while driving around -- both in traditional Grand Prix Races and Knockout Tours, as well as exploring the map in Free Roam.

Mario Kart World is full of Yoshi-themed eateries that include fast food drive-thrus, food trucks, and more, where you will find special item powerups that look like Food Bags instead of the normal Item Block.

Each of the Food Bags is usually regionally themed, and contains different tiers that provide speed boosts (the bigger the food platter, the larger the boost), and will transform your chosen character into a new outfit.

Depending on the regional food, your Character will gain a different outfit that is often related to that region. However, since not all Characters have the same amount of unlockable outfits, not all Food Bags will unlock the same type of outfit across Characters, and some may only provide a speed boost. Creatures like Goombas, Cows, and Dolphins also cannot gain Outfits, and only get speed boosts from Food Bags.

Though the outfit itself is only cosmetic, you'll then unlock it permanently and can be swapped out at will in the Character Select Screen.

Note that you can also set options to disable outfit-swapping when using a Food Bag Powerup.

![Image 1: Tier List](https://kraken.ignimgs.com/_next/static/media/TierList.c19f1c86.svg)

### Mario Kart World: Best Characters Tier List

### Mario Kart World: Best Characters Tier List

All Characters in Mario Kart World
----------------------------------

Mario Kart World contains 24 Main Characters (including Mario, Peach, Bowser, and co.), along with 26 NPC Drivers or Creatures (like the Goomba, Wiggler, Penguin, and so forth) for a total of 50 Racers that you can choose from. However, only 17 Main Characters and 15 Creatures will already be unlocked by default at the start of the game.

To unlock the rest of the cast, you'll need to compete and win different Grand Prix Course Cups to unlock a designated Main Characters.

To unlock other NPC Drivers and Creatures in Mario Kart World, you'll need to become affected by Kamek's transformational power, which is a random item found in an Item Block. Depending on the region you are racing in, Kamek will transform racers into Creatures often found in the area, and getting temporarily transformed will permanently unlock that Creature in the list of Racers you can choose from.

Once just an innocent grazing farm animal with a love of grass, Cow in _Mario Kart_ has certainly “moo-ved” up the ranks in recent times. When you saw cows in [Nintendo’s most popular game of all time](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/ir/en/finance/software/index.html), they were just something to avoid bumping into and they easily faded into the background. While [creative fans have tried to imagine with mods](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QxdwnwUyawk&ab_channel=Raphnin) what would happen if the cow in the background of Moo Moo Meadows _could_ drive a kart, for 30 years, that sort of an idea was just relegated to the world of dreams. Not so in _Mario Kart World_, [the Nintendo Switch 2’s day-one launch title](https://www.inverse.com/gaming/nintendo-mario-kart-world-accessibility-bundle), which features a vast, inter-connected world, several new shiny features — and a huge promotion for Cow.

“In previous Mario Karts, this was really just a background element or even an obstacle,” _Mario Kart World_ producer Kosuke Yabuki tells _Inverse_ in an interview translated from Japanese, “Now this is a playable character, so I imagined that fans of the series from way back would be really happy to see something like that, and that’s our motivation for including it this time.”

Cow, whose pronouns are she/her, has quickly become Mario Kart’s very important character.

Nintendo

The intriguing inclusion came after a brainstorming session the developers had where they were deciding what new Mario Kart characters could be added this time around, and one of the designers sketched a drawing of Cow cruising along a hilariously tiny truck. This addition made the team realize that the formerly non-playable characters of Mario Kart’s backdrops, like the Cheep Cheep fish or cactus-like Pokey, could potentially all drive and compete. A whole new world was unlocked by that realization, [and the developers joked that](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/News/2025/May/Ask-the-Developer-Vol-18-Mario-Kart-World-Chapter-3-2832747.html) Cow completely changed the game for _Mario Kart_, spawning tons of new ideas.

Yabuki says his old way of thinking was that characters needed to have hands and feet to drive karts. But now, characters without any hands or feet, like Goomba and Pokey will be playable, too, so the old rules have gone out the window, he says.

“Maybe I’ve changed my thinking now,” Yabuki says, “Characters like Goomba or Pokey, I probably wouldn’t be able to even explain how they drive exactly, but so long as we’re surprising and delighting people, I think that’s important.”

Cow in _Mario Kart World’s_ free roam photo mode.

Nintendo

Still, in the two months since the _Mario Kart World_ trailer showcased Cow, the developers weren’t prepared for the outpour of support and interest she’s received, spawning plenty of fan art and social media tributes.

“I have to say the reaction really went beyond our imagination in terms of how happy people were and how excited, so that was a wonderful surprise,” Yabuki says. “On release, I’m sure that we’ll see a lot of players choosing to race with Cow or Penguin, but this is still _Mario Kart,_ so I hope that everyone remembers to play Peach and Mario, too.”

#### _Mario Kart World_ releases June 5 on Nintendo Switch 2.

Nintendo Explains How The Cow Became A Playable Character In Mario Kart World

Nintendo Explains How The Cow Became A Playable Character In Mario Kart World
=============================================================================

##### [7 months ago](https://nintendosoup.com/nintendo-explains-how-the-cow-became-a-playable-character-in-mario-kart-world/ "7 months ago") [Iggy](https://nintendosoup.com/author/iggynosuupu/ "View all posts by Iggy") Comments [0 Comment](https://nintendosoup.com/nintendo-explains-how-the-cow-became-a-playable-character-in-mario-kart-world/#respond)

In the first developer interview for Mario Kart World, Nintendo developers shared how the Cow became a playable character in Mario Kart World.

When working on an early version of a course in the game, a sketch of a cow driving a kart came up. This led to character designer quickly putting together a prototype of Cow that could race, which didn’t feel out of place. Nintendo then later expanded the idea to other obstacle characters, such as Cheep Cheep and Pokey. Thanks to the addition of the obstacle drivers, the Kamek item was born, and more obstacle characters were turned into drivers as a result:

> **Now that you mention it, some of the new characters in this game seem like unlikely picks. I was surprised to see Cow as one of the playable characters.**
> 
> **Yabuki**: That’s right. In previous games in the series, Cow was part of the scenery or an obstacle on one of the courses. But when we were working on an early version of a course in this game set on a ranch that players can drive through, this sketch came up. (Laughs)
> 
> **Oh, I thought Cow was just on the back of the truck, but she’s actually driving it. (Laughs)**
> 
> **Ishikawa**: Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that’s when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn’t feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world.
> 
> **Sato**: We called these types of characters “NPC drivers.” In other words, non-player character drivers.
> 
> **Yabuki**: So it was like, “They’re NPCs, but they’re playable? Which is it?” (Laughs) It’s pretty funny to see a four-legged Cow holding onto motorcycle handlebars with her front hooves.
> 
> **Ishikawa**: But when she jumps, she strikes a proper quadrupedal pose. So I’m pretty sure Cow is still in touch with her animal nature. (Laughs)
> 
> **Jikumaru**: It was thanks to the introduction of various “NPC drivers” that the idea to have Kamek appear as an item was born. When Kamek casts a spell, the racers are transformed into playable NPCs, so one by one they might all turn into Cow mid-race. I think it turned out to be a unique item that has never been seen before. In fact, Cow is a character who’s inspired a lot of different ideas, including obstacle characters like Camel and Giraffe.
> 
> **Ishikawa**: Cow is actually a pivotal character in the _Mario Kart_ series. (Laughs)
> 
> **Asahi**: On the other hand, when previously non-playable characters like Cow become playable, it means giving them new ways to express emotion, which must have been difficult for the voice lead. We were conscious of depicting the personalities and characteristics of “NPC drivers” in a way that doesn’t look inferior to classic characters like Mario. The voice team members went through a lot of trial and error in the pursuit of the ideal sound. In addition to more characters, this game also has a wider selection of vehicles for characters to drive, so it was a huge task to create engine sounds that matched the characteristics, such as the appearance and structure, of each vehicle. We tried out a lot of different sounds in our search for something ideal—we even used croaking frogs and beating drums. (Laughs)
> 
> **Sato**: There are a lot of vehicles in this game, too. Since the game is about racing around the world, we’ve included not only race karts, but also everyday vehicles. It must have been tough for the designers, as they had to not only design the body of the vehicle, but also consider how the tires would transform when drifting and how the vehicle would move when jumping.

What do you think? Let us know in the comments.
