----------------------

![Image 39: Mario Kart World screenshot Switch 2](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YMuVhEyuZd68jtnCzNPKaf.jpg)

(Image credit: Nintendo)

According to the [official Nintendo website](https://www.nintendo.com/us/gaming-systems/switch-2/featured-games/mario-kart-world/), the Mario Kart World price is $79.99 in the US. In the UK, the [My Nintendo page](https://nintendo-uk.pxf.io/c/221109/1889570/22585?subId1=grd-gb-1269993281990090044&sharedId=grd-gb&u=https%3A%2F%2Fstore.nintendo.co.uk%2Fen%2Fnintendo-switch-2%3Firclickid%3D0hEX3xWIMxyKUZUSfmzzKUfxUksyhOz2jW3k380%26sharedid%3Dgrd-gb%26irpid%3D221109%26iradtype%3DONLINE_TRACKING_LINK%26utm_medium%3Daffiliate%26utm_source%3Dimpact%26irgwc%3D1) states that the digital edition of the game comes in at £66.99 while the physical version costs £74.99.

This makes Mario Kart World much more expensive than its predecessor, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, with Switch 2 bundles combining with a copy of World coming in at $499.99.

Roll Out With Mario and Friends Across an Interconnected World Featuring Up to 24 Drivers in Grand Prix Races, Chaotic Knockout Tours, Battle Mode, Free Roam and More
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In today’s _Mario Kart World_ Direct presentation, Nintendo unveiled footage detailing new information on the upcoming game – which is set to be the biggest _Mario Kart_ game in series history – launching exclusively for the Nintendo Switch 2 system on June 5. Additionally, a bundle that includes the Nintendo Switch 2 system and a full game download code for the _Mario Kart World_ game will also be available beginning June 5.

[_Mario Kart World_](https://www.nintendo.com/us/gaming-systems/switch-2/featured-games/mario-kart-world/) features a series-first: an interconnected world where you can drive virtually anywhere, including across cities, plains, a desert and even the ocean. Races are held throughout this world’s various regions and feature dynamic weather conditions and a day/night cycle. Start your engines and compete for first place in Grand Prix or the new Knockout Tour mode or simply experience a leisurely drive across a world of diverse locales in Free Roam. The world is your racetrack, and there’s plenty to discover – solo or with friends, locally\* or online\*\*. This is just the starting line!

*   **An Interconnected World:** Drift, draft and drive your way around an interconnected world for the first time in a _Mario Kart_ game. In _Mario Kart World,_ the game’s courses are interspersed across the world with roads leading from one to the next – so players can experience navigating roads in between courses!
    
*   **Grand Prix:** Bring home the gold in Grand Prix, which consists of four different races to win each Cup – including the Mushroom Cup, Flower Cup, Star Cup and more – held across the game’s world. And for the first time in the series, racers will need to drive from one course to the next as part of the Grand Prix! In Mushroom Cup, for example, you’ll start off racing the Mario Bros. Circuit, then the second race will have you covering the distance from Mario Bros. Circuit to Crown City. Conquer every Grand Prix Cup and you might just unlock a certain colorful course!
    
*   **Knockout Tour**: Race from one end of the world to the other in these extended rallies, with checkpoints dotted throughout. If you don’t make the cut, you’re out of the running, so buckle up for these non-stop sprints because you’ll need to keep pace to stay in the race. Your rivals aren’t the only hazards you'll need to avoid on the road, either. Vehicles that shoot Bullet Bills, Hammer Bros. attacks, and other obstacles will find their way into this mode as well. Drive to survive and keep your eyes on first place!
    
*   **Free Roam:** There is plenty to discover in _Mario Kart World_ that goes beyond racing. So when you’re not aiming for first place, take the scenic route in Free Roam! Explore panoramic vistas, go (way) off-road, see the seas and find secrets like hidden coins, or hit P Switches to take on hundreds of missions that can help improve your driving skills outside of races. You can also take in-game photos while free roaming, so take a road trip and strike a pose at the sights.
    
*   **Battle Mode**: Battle Mode is back and more hectic than ever! Secure the gold by collecting the most coins in Coin Runners or burst your rivals’ balloons with items in Balloon Battle. If you pop all of your rival’s balloons, they are out!
    
*   **New Techniques:** Leap over obstacles and more with the new Charge Jump move. Use it to jump onto rails that you can grind, dodge attacks from your rivals and even jump toward a wall to ride on it for a short time. You can also chain together wall-rides to uncover hidden routes. Miss your mark during Free Roam or single-player mode? Just use Rewind to reset your vehicle to its original position – this is a great way to undo a driving mishap, but keep in mind that your rivals will still move normally while rewinding, so try not to lose your lead!
    
*   **24 Racers:** _Mario Kart World_ features races with up to 24 participants from around the world – the most in _Mario Kart_ series history! Modes like Grand Prix and Knockout Tour allow up to 24 players to compete, filling the game world with friends and familiar faces and plenty of rivals to vie for first place.
    
*   **Fun With Everyone, Anywhere:** _Mario Kart World_ offers multiple ways to play together, locally or online. Up to four players can race split screen on the same system. The game also supports local wireless play where up to eight players (with up to two players per Nintendo Switch 2 system) can race together. And players from around the world can join a race or battle in online play. In Free Roam, you can also meet up with your crew anywhere in this game’s world. Drive around, see where your friends are on the map and warp to them instantly. Then race, battle with custom rules or take a road trip to see the sights together.
    
*   **Even More Fun with GameChat:** [GameChat](https://www.nintendo.com/us/gaming-systems/switch-2/features/gamechat/)\*\*\* features an expanded online experience in the _Mario Kart World_ game. Use the Nintendo Switch 2 built-in microphone to voice chat with friends while driving together or take a backseat and watch each other’s game screens. You can enjoy GameChat without needing a Nintendo Switch Online membership until March 31, 2026. After that, a Nintendo Switch Online membership will be required.
    
*   **CameraPlay**: If you have a Nintendo Switch 2 Camera (sold separately)\*\*\*, your face will show up beside your racer, and you can see your friends’ reactions when you play online! When playing locally with family and friends on the same system, a single camera can detect up to four people’s faces that you can see in-game as well.
    
*   **Courses**: _Mario Kart World_ has many races to enjoy across its vast world. Rule the roads on brand new courses like Mario Bros. Circuit, the modern streets of Crown City, the snowy trails of Starview Peak and the spirited Boo Cinema, just to name a few. Nostalgic courses from previous _Mario Kart_ games have also been reimagined to feel at-home within this vast, new world, offering fresh experiences on classics.
    
*   **Characters:** Get behind the wheel as familiar Mushroom Kingdom characters like Mario, Luigi, Peach and Bowser. Looking for a racer that’s a little more offbeat? Try taking Goomba, Spike and even Cow for a test drive.
    
*   **New Items**: Tear up the track with a selection of new and returning items. Throw a Coin Shell to knock rivals off course and make coins appear that gradually increase the speed of whoever collects them. Chill out the competition (and send ’em spinning) with the Ice Flower. Bring down the Hammer to nail your rival or briefly block their path. Use a Mega Mushroom to grow big and squash your rivals. Leap to new heights with the Feather. Call in Kamek’s magic to transform your rivals into something surprising and cause unexpected chaos on the course. The lower your position, the more likely you’ll receive items that could turn the tables, so when you get something good … go for it!
    
*   **Drive-Thru and Roll-Out**: Make a pit stop at Yoshi’s for a local delight: Dash Food! These to-go orders will give you a speed boost and sometimes also unlock outfits that can be donned from the character selection screen. There are plenty of dishes and outfits to find, so drive through when making your way around _Mario Kart World_.
    
*   **Even More Modes**: Whether you want to race or battle, there are even more ways to stoke some friendly competition in _Mario Kart World_. Race against the clock in Time Trials, where players can also go online to compete against ghost data from racers around the world. And you can customize the rules of the road in VS Race, where drivers can decide if they want to compete with two, three or four teams with a classic three-lap ruleset or by driving from one course to another.
    
*   **Roadside Assistance**: Looking for some options to assist you on race day? Features like Smart Steering to keep you on course, Auto-Accelerate and Tilt Controls for motion control steering are available to turn on or off whenever you like. Plus, if you have the Joy-Con 2 Wheel accessory (available as a set of two, sold separately) you can feel like you’re really driving!
    

Remember that Nintendo Switch 2 features [parental controls](https://play.nintendo.com/parents/tools-for-parents/parental-controls/) that let adults manage the content their children can access. For more information about other features, visit [https://www.nintendo.com/switch/](https://www.nintendo.com/us/switch/).

Start your Nintendo Switch™ 2 adventure with this bundle that includes a system and a full game download for the Mario Kart™ World game, exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Nintendo Switch 2 is the next evolution of the Nintendo Switch system—packed with upgrades and fun ways to connect and play together!

**Discover Nintendo Switch 2**   
 Your games will leap to life on the vivid, 7.9” 1080p screen that showcases the system’s powerful processing and graphics performance. The updated dock also supports up to 4K resolution and frame rates up to 120 fps with compatible games and TVs.\*   
   
The reimagined Joy-Con™ 2 controllers snap into place with magnetic connectors—and each controller can even be used as a mouse in compatible games. Plus, you can still enjoy compatible games from your existing Nintendo Switch library\*\*.   
    
**Connect with friends and family with GameChat**   
Once GameChat\*\*\* is set up, press the C Button on your right Joy-Con 2 to start it up, a seamless way to voice chat with your friends, share your game screen, and connect via video chat with a compatible USB-C® camera (sold separately).

Nintendo Switch 2 also has a built-in microphone that filters out noise around you for a clear experience. It’s like hanging out together…from wherever you are.

**GameChat Open-Access Period**  
Until March 31, 2026, GameChat can be used without a Nintendo Switch Online membership. Afterwards, a Nintendo Switch Online membership will be required to use GameChat.   
   
**Start playing right away with Mario Kart World**  
Zip around courses in a vast world where everything is connected in the Mario Kart World game—exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2.

Race along grassy plains, bustling cities, wide-open waters, big ol' volcanos, and more—plus everything in between. Play together on the same system\*\*\*\* with up to 4 players or go for the top spot in online\*\*\* races with up to 24 players.   
   
Start a GameChat session in Mario Kart World and whether you're competing in a race or simply exploring the open road, it's like you're zooming around together.  
   
**Gear up for exclusive games and more**

Nintendo Switch 2 is the exclusive home to games like Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong™ Bananza, and more.

You can also purchase upgrade packs for certain Nintendo Switch games like The Legend of Zelda™: Tears of the Kingdom, Super Mario Party™ Jamboree, and Kirby™ and the Forgotten Land for enhanced experiences and new content!

**Features:**

*   The next evolution of Nintendo Switch™
    
*   One system, three play modes: TV, Tabletop, and Handheld
    
*   Larger, vivid, 7.9” LCD touch screen with support for HDR and up to 120 fps
    
*   Dock that supports 4K when connected to a compatible TV\*
    
*   GameChat\*\* lets you voice chat, share your game screen, and connect via video chat as you play
    
*   256GB internal storage (a portion of which is used by the system), expandable with microSD Express cards (sold separately)

![Image 1: ree](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_e4051ce8a6a84415a1a64ab4173d0a2c~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_147,h_83,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_e4051ce8a6a84415a1a64ab4173d0a2c~mv2.jpg)

**Mario Kart World**

**_Released:_** _June 5th, 2025_

**_Developer:_** _Nintendo_

**_Publisher:_** _Nintendo_

**_Systems:_** _Switch 2_

Mario Kart World looks absolutely gorgeous. Not, say, eighty dollars of gorgeous, but it’s a beautiful game.

Whatever balls Nintendo could be accused of dropping with the Switch 2, it cannot be said they made a poor choice of game when it came to showing the system’s graphical potential. Some of the choices made _with_ that game may be a little more contentious.

![Image 2: More than tires are gonna get flat.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_0ae8446029284886bf24332af0050500~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_0ae8446029284886bf24332af0050500~mv2.png)

_More than tires are gonna get flat._

I’ll gladly admit it upfront - as the game to introduce a new normal of publishers charging $80 (minimum) for games, Mario Kart World is something I can’t help but resent. While many people will access the game as part of a console bundle, Nintendo’s nonetheless leveraging a beloved series to acquire blanket permission for some distasteful bullshit.

This will influence reviews going forward, and I shall be holding games with a $79.99 base price to a _far_ higher standard. If companies think they deserve to charge such an exceptional rate, their games better damn well _be_ exceptional. If you think this is an unfair policy, feel free to stop reading.

![Image 3: That's just Cheep.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_5ba8df507bed42b19ecd682567b30ca7~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_5ba8df507bed42b19ecd682567b30ca7~mv2.png)

_That's just Cheep._

Mario Kart World is pretty damn good - not _exceptional_, but it’s got that baseline level of quality one expects from a Mario Kart game. It’s also an inherently more chaotic breed of Mario Kart, one that series fans have had to adjust to.

With a whopping 24 racers in play and more items flying around than ever before, Mario Kart World is a family friendly bloodbath. There are plenty of opportunities to show off skillful driving, especially with all the acrobatics one can pull off, but finesse often surrenders the wheel to Lady Luck, and in a game full of Mega Mushrooms, Luck’s a bitch.

Not that I’m complaining about the whims of chance - I’ve been winning more races than ever before.

![Image 4: Clawed my way to the top.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_a29a95c099104e2283641489d8696fd7~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_a29a95c099104e2283641489d8696fd7~mv2.png)

_Clawed my way to the top._

A lot’s crammed into Mario Kart World when it comes to raw assets. The huge roster of racers welcomes a number of debuts - including a surprising increase of mook representation, which I’m a big fan of. As someone whose favorites have always been Dry Bones and Shy Guy, I’m delighted to have the likes of Cheep Cheep, Spike, and Sidestepper joining in.

Nintendo taketh away as well as giveth, because Nintendo is Nintendo, so some faces haven’t returned - this includes the Koopalings, which I’m personally bummed out by. After Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, it’s hard not to notice what’s missing, especially when it comes to the crossover content that’s no longer there. Considering the bump in price, it’ll sting if Nintendo’s going to sell characters like Link and the Inkling as DLC.

![Image 5: Use items to get some Wiggle room. ](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_b041eb49cce84e69b8e929bf0d280505~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_b041eb49cce84e69b8e929bf0d280505~mv2.png)

_Use items to get some Wiggle room._

Some new items join the usual assortment, including a golden shell that blitzes down the center of the road and drops coins along the way, a Hammer that rapidly lays obstacles down in an overheard arc, and the Mega Mushroom, by far one of the most impactful new additions - you will learn to both love _and_ curse the power to squash rivals.

There’s also Kamek, who transforms racers into those mook characters, an Ice Flower to compliment the Fire Flower, and a Feather that’s used to bounce over hazards. Overall, a solid assortment of new toys, but I’m not really excited by any of them. Also the Golden Shell is just crap.

![Image 6: Boned and railed.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_6e0c71164a30467cbb914303b64732b4~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_6e0c71164a30467cbb914303b64732b4~mv2.png)

_Boned and railed._

Maneuverability is a big part of World’s gameplay, with additional ways of getting around that provide some fun visual spectacle. A proper jump is now part of the basic toolkit, pulled off by briefly charging a hop. You can use this to temporarily ride along nearby walls, and you’ll get a short boost when you jump back onto the road. It’s not always optimal, but it _is_ quite fun.

You can also grind along certain surfaces, with plenty of railings and such scattered around for you to slide along. As with wall karting, it’s not practical in every situation, but I can’t help going out of my way to grind because it’s so neat. Naturally, there are some areas cleverly designed with the acrobatic racer in mind, providing plenty of opportunities for kart-based parkor.

![Image 7: There's a lot of water in this one, and it looks lovely.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_efd45b1232664b92ab941aa83e01206c~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_efd45b1232664b92ab941aa83e01206c~mv2.png)

_There's a lot of water in this one, and it looks lovely._

Alongside the usual bunch of game modes, Mario Kart World introduces Knockout Tour, which has become my favorite way to play. It’s an eliminator that shaves the player count down from 24 to a final 4 via intermittent checkpoints. Given the changes to some of Mario Kart’s dynamics, it’s clear Knockout Tour is _meant_ to be the main attraction, as it’s best suited to World’s increased level of anarchy.

Of course, regular races, Battle Mode, and Grand Prix are still there, but I have spent most of my time doing Knockout runs. They start out as low stakes fun and get gradually more enthralling with each checkpoint. Winning these Tours have been some of the most excitement I’ve had with the series.

Knockout Tour is also a good way to showcase Mario Kart World’s big gimmick.

![Image 8: So much world, so little spice.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_7960b16e29eb4896b62dccff23b183ee~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_7960b16e29eb4896b62dccff23b183ee~mv2.png)

_So much world, so little spice._

Said gimmick is in the title, with every track placed on a large interconnected world. It’s a fun idea, and there’s no denying how impressively big the thing is. I love how every playable character is placed on the map to give the impression they’re constantly riding around in real time.

This interconnectivity exacts a price when it comes to the specific identity of individual courses - I couldn’t tell you a favorite stage off the top of my head since they all bleed into each other. Much of the connective area between courses is rather mundane too, some of it just being straight stretches of plain motorway. Races are prone to spotty pacing, a lot of flavorless driving with comparative short bursts of creativity.

That’s not to say there aren’t memorable parts, but that’s exactly what they are - portions of an overall world rather than standout stages with their own presence.

![Image 9: How?](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_549ca81dd1fa408dab703ffb6b9a4f86~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_549ca81dd1fa408dab703ffb6b9a4f86~mv2.png)

_How?_

I’d say the tradeoff would be worth it if the “open world” we got in return was a lot more exciting than it is. A large, explorable Mario Kart sandbox is my idea of a _fantastic_ time - open design is one of my favorite concepts for a racing game, and if any series is suited for it, it’s this one.

Despite all the potential, however, just a little time spent in Free Roam exposes how little interest Nintendo seems to have had in making the most of the idea. I keep _wanting_ to freely explore the world, but the sheer lack of stuff to do inspires almost no enthusiasm.

If you _adore_ checkpoint races you’ll be in Heaven, but those expecting much more will find only disappointment. Aside from dozens of variants of checkpoint challenges, Mario Kart’s titular world offers some collectibles, the occasional Nabbit to chase, a few Boomerang Bro racers to try and frustratedly hit with Green Shells, and if I can remember anything else I’ll let you know.

![Image 10: Oh, there's also Blue Coin challenges aka freeform checkpoint racing!](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_0a74c9363cbb47968c95c6b89fe3afc3~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_0a74c9363cbb47968c95c6b89fe3afc3~mv2.png)

_Oh, there's also Blue Coin challenges aka freeform checkpoint racing!_

With no way to mark locations on a map and only a handful of borderline useless telescope stations serving as navigation tools, locating activities across the vast environment is a matter of driving around and fighting boredom. You can spend a long time actively looking for stuff to do in Free Roam and come up short.

Don’t worry too much about completing challenges though - Mario Kart World’s idea of a reward system is complete and utter _wank_. Your efforts are almost always recognized with a sticker, a little logo you can affix next to your username for online players to take zero notice of because they’re tiny and uninteresting. That’s all you get for pretty much any activity that requires effort.

![Image 11: Trans rides.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_62126e0db4db41c4892a4824f16dfdd1~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_62126e0db4db41c4892a4824f16dfdd1~mv2.png)

_Trans rides._

Why can’t you unlock new vehicles, characters, or costumes via these open world challenges? Because each type of unlockable is bound to one single method of acquisition, and mixing things up would be too interesting. Characters are tied to Grand Prix completion, karts are earned in a linear order via the acquisition of coins, and costumes are earned by having the relevant racer pick up a food item and eat it.

Kamek is about the only interesting way to get something, and that’s simply due to how utterly random he is.

![Image 12: No outfits for Dry Bones? Dry BOOOO!](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_fb3349ea6d6d4e57910fc482386a23a7~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_fb3349ea6d6d4e57910fc482386a23a7~mv2.png)

_No outfits for Dry Bones? Dry BOOOO!_

I find the singular and entirely unfun process of unlocking outfits particularity aggravating. There’s such a distinct lack of spontaneity, surprise, and reward to just switching characters and having them use the same items over and over. New cosmetics would be the _perfect_ incentive for engaging with an open world, yet Nintendo couldn’t have been less adventurous about it.

Also, why are outfits treated as entirely separate racers instead of skins like they used to be? What is the benefit of clogging up the character selection menu that much? Seriously, I could write an entire essay on World’s costume fumblings alone.

![Image 13: My face when I'm in the lead too early.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_e3e6378804d744099935447e1ec87844~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_e3e6378804d744099935447e1ec87844~mv2.png)

_My face when I'm in the lead too early._

Anyway, as I’ve suggested at certain points, Mario Kart World is absolute mayhem.

The increased impact items have on races cannot be understated. It’s not uncommon to shoot from last to first place and vice versa in an instant. While this means no race feels truly lost until it’s very almost over, it also means anybody in the lead is more fragile than ever, to such a degree that trying to have a _race_ sometimes feels counter to winning a _race_.

More items than ever are prepped to batter you from behind, and they _will_. Rarely will you ever just take a hit and cede some ground - more commonly you’ll get knocked by one thing into another thing, which will slow you down enough to perpetuate a daisy chain of bullshit from other things.

![Image 14: Bullets are lifesavers (in Mario Kart).](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_746bfd17ad84491fbea399312e59f5f0~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_746bfd17ad84491fbea399312e59f5f0~mv2.png)

_Bullets are lifesavers (in Mario Kart)._

I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve been toppled and squashed several times within a matter of nanoseconds, dragged from top to bottom with zero ability to negate it. Conversely, I’ve sped from the bottom to the top just as easily thanks to how damn powerful every mushroom-based boost is. It’s easy to surge ahead, but _staying_ ahead is another thing entirely.

Common convention’s always held that whoever’s in the lead gets limited item access and has to fear the devastating Blue Shell as a form of balance. With Mario Kart World, however, I’m wondering if Nintendo has focused so heavily on players in the back half of a race that there’s almost no viable way left for the front half to defend itself. Perhaps, after all these years, the scales have tipped a bit _too_ far?

![Image 15: They're coming to get you.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_c579f676d5b44a6baa3c71767ea097e2~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_c579f676d5b44a6baa3c71767ea097e2~mv2.png)

_They're coming to get you._

It’s telling that, whenever I’m in the lead, I’m not even afraid of the Blue Shell anymore - that’s just part of the overall noise. _Wherever_ I’m placed, my fear is the same - all I worry about is not getting dragged to the bottom of the bucket by the gaggle of crabs all around me.

I want to emphasize that I don’t think it’s _not_ a fun way to play. It’s sheer anarchy, and it certainly levels the playing field in its own inelegant way. The final stretch on the way to victory is _terrifying_ now, and the relief when one crosses the finish is consequently elating. However, it can lead to some truly disheartening outcomes over which your influence feels negligible.

![Image 16: Dynamic weather is a nice touch.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_5ea371f14e5a4e17acf83abdbe8032f9~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_5ea371f14e5a4e17acf83abdbe8032f9~mv2.png)

_Dynamic weather is a nice touch._

One element can _absolutely_ fuck off, and that’s the overbearing “course correction” of Lakitu. In previous games, he could always be relied on to fish players out of chasms or put them back on the road if they veered off, but for some reason he’s _way_ overtuned in World.

He’ll grab you if you step even a _tiny_ bit off course, confiscating any item you have in the process. It’s so bad that you won’t even know _why_ he’s yanking you away sometimes - at one point I was literally on the course, having steered down towards a ramp while in flight mode, but the game interpreted my move as me… _falling_? I guess? Who knows?

Lakitu has served Mario Kart well all these years, but he’s turned into a right cloudy cunt.

![Image 17: Here comes a moo challenger.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_4dc0100be1df44aabaa9146c73a6539e~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_4dc0100be1df44aabaa9146c73a6539e~mv2.png)

_Here comes a moo challenger._

Mario Kart World’s presentation is truly impeccable. The saturated colors are my perfect type of eye-searing beauty, and there are so many lovely environmental details. Despite the lack of activities, a lot has been done to make sectors of the world you’d not really see outside Free Roam at least _look_ lively, with all sorts of characters and creatures wandering around.

Everything is backed by a truly fantastic selection of music. Catchy tunes, big brassy sounds, a ton of nostalgia thrown in for good measure, I’ve not a bad word to say about the soundtrack.

![Image 18: All of the colors!](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_b37195da45d441ce95a08ade34510723~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_b37195da45d441ce95a08ade34510723~mv2.png)

_All of the colors!_

The visual design of karts is absolutely top notch. I’m not just saying that because there’s a lobster bike, but also _there’s a fucking lobster bike_! I wish the actual process of unlocking vehicles was more varied and interesting, because the vehicles themselves are really cool and deserve more exciting methods of acquisition.

Mario Kart World is a strange one. It’s provided some of the most fun I’ve had with the series, yet it’s also left me feeling underwhelmed at regular intervals. It offers a huge amount of fresh cool stuff, but still manages to shortchange players in major ways. Mostly, it lets itself down by promising an exciting open world but delivering a flimsy cardboard one that looks incredible but offers very little to do.

![Image 19: Sweet ride.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/a511ef_c5060afbbcc5425080e5927c5c77ab26~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_49,h_28,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/a511ef_c5060afbbcc5425080e5927c5c77ab26~mv2.png)

_Sweet ride._

A lot of flash and _some_ substance, it’s a very fun game in a package that doesn’t live up to its massive potential, much less the massive price tag it’s introduced to mainstream gaming.

**7/10**

33.content:
#### Developed by: Nintendo EPD  
Published by: Nintendo  
Platforms: Nintendo Switch 2  
Release Date: Out Now!

* * *

Back in June, the launch line-up of the Nintendo Switch 2 was understandably dominated by _Mario Kart World_. This is the first brand new _Mario Kart_ on consoles since _Mario Kart 8_ on Wii U back in 2014 (the Switch received an upgraded version, _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, in 2017, which I skipped) – so at least for me personally, it’s felt a long time coming. Mixed in with the excitement of a brand new Nintendo console, it made the launch of _Mario Kart World_ feel like a real event, especially when played with friends, which is where _Mario Kart_ always excels.

Over the past couple of months, I’ve played a fair amount of _Mario Kart World_, in various different configurations: both on the TV and in handheld, in solo, local co-op, and online with a friend. Now, I’ve reached a point where I feel I can state a comprehensive opinion on the game, having experienced both the racing modes and the open world that’s a major selling point of this iteration of _Mario Kart_. My thoughts are overall very positive, but there are also some flawed aspects to the game – but I’ll expand upon this more later on in the review. Without further ado then, let’s get into it!

* * *

Start Your Engines
------------------

Perhaps it was the new-console glow, or perhaps it was that wait since _Mario Kart 8_, but launching into _Mario Kart World_ for the first time felt distinctly special. The game encourages you straight into exploring the open world first; this consists of the various tracks connected by open spaces of road, field, water, desert, and more. What’s immediately remarkable about the game is just how gorgeous it looks, both in handheld but also especially when played on a 4K HDR TV – and whilst this isn’t new technology, it’s wonderful to play Nintendo games in such high fidelity via the Switch 2. The visual direction of _Mario Kart World_ makes brilliant use of the new hardware, presenting a world full of vibrancy, colour, and personality – which is shown in the track designs, whether it’s the bustling Shy Guy Bazaar, the scrumptious Sky-High Sundae, or the fiery Bowser’s Castle, just to name three!

![Image 1](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mkw_sgb_view.jpg?w=1024)

![Image 2](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_03.jpg?w=1024)

![Image 3](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_17.jpg?w=1024)

The infused personality is evident in the roster of characters (complete with various different unlockable outfits). Returning are your usual suspects like Mario, Luigi, Peach, and so forth; additionally, there are plenty of newcomers, including minor enemies such as Konkdor and Cataquack, and even bit-part characters such as Dolphin and, of course, Cow! If you’ve seen any discourse about _Mario Kart World_ since the initial announcement, you’ll know that the Cow and their adorable grin has captured the attention of the internet, and I’ve had a wonderful time watching the various memes and edits their inclusion has spawned.

Many of the characters have a range of changeable outfits too, which are unlocked by collecting Dash Food bags from vendors in races or the open world. It adds an extra way to differentiate the characters, ranging from punk rock biker looks to desert outfits and much more in between – and they can be combined with the plentiful different karts and bikes to create the aesthetic you’re looking for. A Photo Mode has been added in tandem with this, giving plentiful options for taking pictures that show off the world and characters as you see fit. Me being me, I’m sad that we got an Explorer outfit Toad but no actual Captain Toad… But there’s always time for that in DLC, hopefully!

[![Image 4](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldyoshi.png?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldyoshi.png)

_A smorgasbord of Yoshi! Or Yoshis? Yoshies?_

The attention to detail in both audio and graphic effects is especially apparent when you build up speed. Karts and bikes camber side-to-side when they hop and drift; tyres are spongey and visibly bounce and recoil according to the track surface; and sparks crackle off your vehicle as you drift and build up a boost, just to name a small handful of the details I’m talking about. I particularly like the tension of drifting around the sharpest corners, with the screen often tilting with you and making it extra satisfying to hit the apex. Plus, the music is noticeably exceptional, supplying a consistently energetic chorus that accentuates the gameplay – especially in the final unlockable tracks, which supply a climactic crescendo unlike any other I’ve experienced in _Mario Kart_. Overall, the whole experience is lifted by this pristine look and feel, whether it’s the relatively laid-back open world, or the competitive modes, where the palpable sense of momentum is most gripping.

* * *

It’s a Knockout!
----------------

Despite the “World” being a key selling point of the game, it’s still those core competitive modes that retained the tightest grip on my attention. Whilst the expected familiar selection of Grand Prix, custom VS, Battle, and Time Trial modes are all here, the game deserves credit for also introducing a brand new main mode to go alongside Grand Prix. This goes by the name of Knockout Tour, where 6 different tracks are combined together into one extra-long race. It takes advantage of the increased count of 24 racers to introduce checkpoint gates along the way, eliminating those at the back each time. Essentially, it’s a way of introducing popular battle royale-esque sensibilities into _Mario Kart_, and it creates a very fun sense of chaos – especially in local multiplayer, when your friends and you are desperately trying to stay in the race amidst the various items flying around!

[![Image 5](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_36.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_36.jpg)

_A road trip across the Mushroom Kingdom! Thankfully, less traffic jams than real life_

Knockout Tours are arguably the biggest challenge awaiting completionist solo players in _Mario Kart World_. It’s classic knowledge now that to get the maximum 3-star rating in Grand Prix, you need to win all four races; but in Knockout Tour, you need to be leading through every single checkpoint! This is an extremely tough task, as it necessitates not just victory, but to be consistently leading – even despite homing Red Shells, or the dreaded blue Spiny Shells that target the leader. I set myself the personal challenge of 3-starring every Knockout Tour, and it led to many failed attempts, but it was highly satisfying when I finally achieved that goal. For _Mario Kart_ veterans, it’s a good addition to have a target that takes this extra level of dedication to complete.

I just mentioned the items and the chaos synonymous with _Mario Kart World_ – and that side of the game is just as entertaining (and frustrating) as ever before! To me, _Mario Kart_ is similar to other games such as _Super Smash Bros._ because at their core, each iteration is built on the same gameplay loop, and it makes it tough to critique a new entry – on one hand, it’d be unwise to stray too far from what makes the series so immensely popular, but on the other, there has to be enough new ideas to justify a new game that still feels imaginative.

[![Image 6](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_32.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_32.jpg)

[![Image 7](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_33.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_33.jpg)

[![Image 8](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_35.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_35.jpg)

As aforementioned, the Knockout Tours are a standout way in which _Mario Kart World_ achieves the latter, and some of these ideas bleed over into Grand Prix, where you don’t just drive around four tracks – instead, after the first race, the initial laps are rolling starts, as you drive across the world to the next track, road-trip style. It’s a neat way to keep the same formula but match it to the open-world aesthetic of _Mario Kart World_ – and in VS there are options to play either in this mode, or with the traditional laps, catering to either preference.

Further to this, there are tweaks to the racing itself, the most notable arguably being the new parkour/trick abilities. If you drive up onto a rail, you can grind along it and perform extra trick boosts, and you can even trick onto a wall and wall-ride along it, which opens up jaw-dropping shortcuts if you master this ability (there are plenty of astonishing clips doing the rounds online)! On top of this, drifting boosts can now be used in a straight line, and launch you off the ground slightly to help initiate some of these parkour moves. In combination, all these extra options elevate the height of the skill ceiling, and keep _Mario Kart World_ engaging for those who have mastered previous entries in the series. Crucially, it does this without losing the accessibility as a go-to local multiplayer party game – the extra skills are a cherry on top for those who want to go above and beyond, but they’re not essential for winning races against the CPU.

[![Image 9](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_19.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_19.jpg)

_Boo Cinema is another standout track, which applies a film filter to part of the course_

Items are one of the infamous levellers of _Mario Kart_, and there have been some tweaks and additions on this front too. Your usual roster of shells, bananas, and mushrooms, and more are all here, although it’s noticeable that the raw power of items such as Bullet Bill have been slightly softened, perhaps to accommodate the new racer count of 24. Some of the notable new items include the golden Coin Shell, which leaves a trail of coins behind it, and the feather, which leaps you into the air, opening another opportunity to perform tricks, wallrides, and other shortcuts. To more literally aid more inexperienced players, there are still the helpful options for motion controls, auto-accelerate, and driving aids. Whilst these aren’t new, they’re still great to see return, and are often essential for balanced 4-player sessions that everyone can enjoy!

* * *

Give Me a Boost
---------------

As fun as _Mario Kart_ can be in solo play, multiplayer is where the series has always shined brightest, and that continues to be the case for _World_. I’ve had the opportunity to play with several combinations of friends, and the game has impressively accommodated their varying levels of _Mario Kart_ experience each time, whether they’re a fresh newcomer or someone who’s been away from the series for a while. It’s easy to criticize the items when they’re hitting you, but they do a great job at helping those towards the back stay with the pack, and there’s still the option to use items such as shells and bananas defensively whilst in the lead.

[![Image 10](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_30.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_30.jpg)

_Expect to shout at your friends – in a pleasant way, of course_

Local multiplayer has consistently resulted in a brilliant time, complete with the playful shouting, cheers, and competitive back-and-forth that you hope for from _Mario Kart_ – so I can report that it’s a success in that department! My favourite local multiplayer option is the extended custom VS modes, which have plenty of customisable options, including speed, difficulty, item frequency, and the amount of races, which go up to 32 at a time. As a big Formula 1 fan, I love to nerd out about the accumulated points and the drama of how the final standings will end up, so VS will inevitably become my most-played mode!

In terms of online play, _Mario Kart World_ doesn’t quite hit the same heights as local multiplayer, because of that lack of immediate in-person reaction – and whilst it’s admirable that Nintendo has added chat functionality, I did end up defaulting to using a Discord call instead, because of the familiarity and ease of use. The main motivation to play online is to raise your versus rating (VR), which is essentially the same system we had way back on _Mario Kart Wii_. In my opinion, it’s disappointing that Nintendo hasn’t added more reasons to play online, especially in a gaming landscape where online games consistently add new modes, tournaments, and other rewards for playing consistently. The end result is that I quickly fell off of online multiplayer, and have focused mostly on solo and local multiplayer.

[![Image 11](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_27.jpg?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartworld_27.jpg)

_Driving on water supplies opportunity to perform tricks as you bounce over the waves_

Furthermore, I found that the returning Battle Mode was most ideal for multiplayer – in _World_, there are two options, Balloon Battle and Coin Runners, which will be familiar to players of previous _Mario Kart_ games. Balloon Battle gives you five balloons to protect whilst doing your best to hit opponents and earn points for removing their balloons, and Coin Runners has you searching for as many coins as you can, whilst again attempting to hit others and remove their coins (whilst avoiding them doing the same to you). I have to say, I’ve never been a huge Battle Mode fan over the years, and this version hasn’t changed that – but conversely, if you love Battle Mode, this will fill that quota well. My main disappointment is that the modes are time-based instead of score-based, as I generally prefer having that concrete target and the tension of seeing who can reach it first. Despite my criticisms, I am glad Battle Mode is back, as it offers a welcome change of pace from the racing modes.

* * *

Free as a Birdo
---------------

Of course, a major differentiator for _Mario Kart World_ is the inclusion of a free roam mode, where you can explore the tracks (and the spaces between them) at your leisure. There’s certainly an immediate novelty to this – I have nostalgic memories of _LEGO Racers 2_, which I played a lot on PC as a child, and included a similar experience of exploring an open world between races in a colourful, family-friendly world. My hope was that _Mario Kart World_ might recapture that whimsical feeling, and supply a world with plenty of secrets and rewards, and most importantly motivation to find them. At first, _World_ is successful in this; one of my earliest ventures was rocking up to the Dino Dino Jungle area, and visiting the inner laboratory/auditorium section. With precise driving and the careful use of tricks, you can make your way to the top of this area – which is thrilling the first time, but soon the realisation kicks in that there’s a lack of reason to do so.

[![Image 12](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroampeachcoin.png?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroampeachcoin.png)

[![Image 13](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroamquestionmarkpanel.png?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroamquestionmarkpanel.png)

[![Image 14](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroambluecoins.png?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroambluecoins.png)

When in free roam, _Mario Kart World_ has an uncanny sense of emptiness, and it’s partly because that palpable sense of forward energy – which is so prevalent in the competitive modes – is gone, without being replaced by much else. It’s not that there isn’t anything to do in the open world – for example, there are Peach Medallions and Question Mark Panels to find, as well as P Switches that activate various challenges – but the problem is that there isn’t much motivation to track all these things down. The main rewards are stickers, which are small graphic icons you can attach next to your profile name, and feel inconsequential. More work needed to be done to make the world feel alive, and not just like a suspended state of limbo from the Grand Prix mode.

The Toads and Shy Guys milling around and making campfires are a great touch, but they’re another short-lived novelty that doesn’t add substance to the experience of navigating the open world. It’s fun to find items and complete challenges, but they’re incredibly scattered – and whilst there’s a tracker for the Question Mark Panels, there’s curiously no in-game indicator for how many Medallions or Switches are left to find (and also no statistics or records screen for other modes, either). On the other hand, something free roam does do well is increasing the level of awe the world has. You can travel a long way out into the ocean, and discover sea dragons, whales, and more, and I had a great time inspecting the scale of impressive courses such as DK Spaceport. As mentioned at the start of the review, _Mario Kart World_ is a stunning game to look at and listen to, and the open world gives you more time to do just that.

[![Image 15](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroamring.png?w=1024)](https://wcrobinson.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1600px-mkworldfreeroamring.png)

_P Switch challenges often consist of time trials_

However, it’s a great shame that there’s no formal splitscreen multiplayer for the open world – there’s a partial workaround, by loading into an empty wireless mode lobby, but challenges are turned off, and it’s not at all optimal. In a game marketed on free roam, and in a series known for local multiplayer, it’s a disappointing oversight that significantly reduces the reason to play this way. I have occasionally played free roam in single-player as a laid-back secondary experience, for example when listening to a podcast or talking to friends – but it has untapped potential as a playground for friends to enjoy together, and honestly, I think this would’ve papered over many of my problems with the emptiness of the open world. Instead, more often than not, you’ll launch straight into Grand Prix, Knockout Tour, or VS, as that is where the most joyous parts of _Mario Kart World_ reside.

* * *

Final Thoughts
--------------

Coming to the end of this review, I’m aware that I’ve flagged multiple issues I have with _Mario Kart World_ – so I need to re-emphasize that this is a genuinely excellent _Mario Kart_ game, that not only delivers the best-looking and best-sounding entry into the series, but has multiple new ideas and modes that make it feel distinct. Changeable character outfits, new trick mechanics, and especially the Knockout Tour mode supply fresh style that have made _World_ my new go-to local multiplayer game, and a game I’ve spent many an enjoyable hour in by myself as well. The main disappointment has to be the free roam mode, which feels sparse and quickly struggles to retain player attention – and I really hope that in the future, Nintendo supports the game with additional content that fills out this world more. Alternatively, add Captain Toad to the playable characters, and I’ll probably be happy, haha! In all seriousness, _Mario Kart World_ definitely has flaws, but the core racing experience is dazzling, and it’s a superb way to start the Switch 2 era!

8.5/10
------

![Image 2: mario, luigi, donkey kong, yoshi, and princess peach in mario kart world free roam mode](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/hero-image.fill.size_1248x702.v1749859110.jpg)

*   Great racing action

*   Knockout Tour is a blast
*   Races are more chaotic
*   GameChat enhances the fun factor

The Bad

*   Open world doesn't have a lot going on
*   Online features could be more fleshed out

[![Image 3: Mashable Selects](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/series/00qt89JRmqMMqSNoQqkpGd9/logo.fill.size_400x400.v1683133008.png)](https://mashable.com/series/mashable-selects)

After careful hands-on testing, we feature our favorite gear and gadgets as Mashable Selects products in our dedicated shopping guides.

* * *

[_Mario Kart World_](https://mashable.com/article/3-new-mario-kart-world-features-switch-2-grind), the lone original flagship launch title for the [Nintendo Switch 2](https://mashable.com/article/nintendo-switch-2-launch-retailer-guide-restock-tracker-june-12), is as much defined by what it is as what it is not.

What it _is_ is a tremendously fun _Mario Kart_ game that hones the franchise’s trademark fun to a hilarious, borderline sadistic, and nearly scientifically perfect degree. What it’s _not_ is a revolutionary open-world epic on par with the Switch 1’s biggest launch title, [_The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild_](https://mashable.com/article/legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild-review), or even other open-world racers like _Burnout Paradise_ and _Forza Horizon_.

Do not create a game in your head that doesn’t exist; this is a kick-ass _Mario Kart_ game that happens to have an open world in it. Whether that’s enough for you to want to buy a Switch 2 at launch or not is your business, not mine. While _Mario Kart World_ doesn’t necessarily live up to the seemingly infinite potential of an open-world _Mario Kart_ game, it lives up to my expectations as a longtime fan of the series who really, really enjoys playing it online, which in turn makes it a great showcase for what makes the Switch 2 awesome.

You can get _Mario Kart World_ for $79 at [Walmart](https://zdcs.link/z3GGmV?pageview_type=Standard&template=review&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Walmart&object_type=review&object_uuid=02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC&short_url=z3GGmV&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Freview%2Fmario-kart-world-review "(opens in a new window)") (and $79.99 at [Nintendo](https://zdcs.link/QGggOW?pageview_type=Standard&template=review&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Nintendo&object_type=review&object_uuid=02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC&short_url=QGggOW&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Freview%2Fmario-kart-world-review "(opens in a new window)")), or you can try to find the [Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle](https://zdcs.link/z3GGmV?pageview_type=Standard&template=review&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Nintendo%20Switch%202%20%2B%20Mario%20Kart%20World%20Bundle&object_type=review&object_uuid=02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC&short_url=z3GGmV&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Freview%2Fmario-kart-world-review "(opens in a new window)").

[![Image 4: nintendo switch 2 mario kart world](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-9.fill.size_256x144.v1749859111.jpg) Opens in a new window](https://zdcs.link/z3GGmV?pageview_type=Standard&template=review&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=image&element_label=image&object_type=review&object_uuid=02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC&short_url=z3GGmV&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Freview%2Fmario-kart-world-review "(opens in a new window)")

Check prices at Walmart

[Shop Now](https://zdcs.link/z3GGmV?pageview_type=Standard&template=review&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=buy-button&element_label=Get%20Deal&object_type=review&object_uuid=02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC&short_url=z3GGmV&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Freview%2Fmario-kart-world-review "(opens in a new window)")

You can also read my full [hands-on deep dive on the Switch 2](https://mashable.com/review/nintendo-switch-2-review), but in the meantime, let's get into my _Mario Kart World_ review.

_Mario Kart World_ may not be what you expect
---------------------------------------------

![Image 5: Mario Kart Knockout Tour screenshot](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1749757157.png)

Knockout Tour is the real highlight here. Credit: Nintendo

Back in April, when Nintendo [first detailed _Mario Kart World_ to the masses](https://mashable.com/article/switch-2-nintendo-direct-everything-announced), plenty of folks (myself included) became wide-eyed with awe in thinking about what an open-world _Mario Kart_ game could be. _Mario Kart World_ is not quite that.

To be clear, after a week of extensive play, I don’t think that’s a bad thing, but it is disappointing, especially if you tuned out the [later marketing](https://mashable.com/article/mario-kart-world-direct-livestream-reactions) that made it explicitly clear that the free roam feature is a goofy little side mode and not the main attraction. It’s an easy way to unlock new costumes for characters, and it’s full of little bespoke challenges to complete, but their rewards pretty much only come in the form of stickers, which don’t actually do anything meaningful. Those challenges are only worth doing for the love of the game, in other words.

_Mario Kart World_’s biggest surprise, then, is how much that doesn’t really bother me. Once the final game was in my hands, I realized the open world exists to justify the modes you just pick from a menu. Grand prix races ask players to race between tracks, for instance. The new Knockout Tour mode, which is the game’s biggest highlight, takes players on a _Cannonball Run_\-esque (that’s a reference the kids will get) cross-country race, in which those at the back of the pack are gradually eliminated from contention over time.

![Image 6: Mario Kart World screenshot of the Knockout Tour selection screen](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-2.fill.size_2000x1125.v1749757157.png)

There are several Knockout Tour stretches available. Credit: Nintendo

SEE ALSO: [Switch 2 smashes Nintendo's own record, selling 3.5 million consoles](https://mashable.com/article/nintendo-switch-2-sales-record)

It’s tempting to call the open world “tacked-on,” but I would argue that's not really appropriate. The idea that all of these tracks are physically connected to one another is baked into the design of the major modes; Knockout Tour wouldn’t exist without the open world, therefore, the existence of the open world is justified. That said, since this is a _Mario Kart World_ review, it’s worth noting that most tracks can be turned into regular three-lap circuits during multiplayer races, if you prefer that.

Still, I don’t want to let Nintendo entirely off the hook here. Free roam _should_ be more rewarding than it is. Stickers are not a good enough incentive to complete P-switch challenges, many of which are genuinely pretty difficult. That being said, _Mario Kart World_ is a ton of fun on its own merits, regardless of what you may or may not wish it was instead.

But the part where it’s _Mario Kart_ might be better than ever
--------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 7: Mario Kart World screenshot of Mario and Luigi facing off against each other](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-3.fill.size_2000x1125.v1749757157.png)

The races are great. Credit: Nintendo

Once you process and get over the fact that this isn’t _Burnout Paradise_ with blue shells, _Mario Kart World_ rocks. The sorcerers over at Nintendo have found a bunch of ways to make the races more frenetic, chaotic, and arguably fun than ever.

For starters, there are now 24 competitors per race, rather than the traditional 12. That means the beginning portion of every race is kind of a nightmare, in a great way. There’s just a mass of humanity (and cows, and dolphins, and Goombas, and anything else that’s ever been in a Mario game) all trying to knock each other out. If you’re inclined to get mad at the part of _Mario Kart_ where sometimes you get hit by a shell that you couldn’t do anything about, get ready for twice as much of that.

I’m not inclined to get mad about that because I think it makes _Mario Kart_ more interesting than many other racing games. If I wanted to play a game where mere driving prowess was enough to win on its own, I would play almost any other racing game. I find comfort in the idea that sometimes you can be perfect, and it’s still not good enough because of some nonsense that was out of your control. That’s just life, man.

Crucially, it’s also _very_ funny to go from first to 20th in about three seconds. Learning to laugh at yourself is key to enjoying _Mario Kart_.

![Image 8: Donkey Kong in Mario Kart World](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-4.fill.size_2000x1125.v1749757157.png)

Donkey Kong rocks. Credit: Nintendo

With that in mind, though, the driving mechanics here are maybe my favorite in any _Mario Kart_. It still works roughly the same on the surface as it did in _Mario Kart 8_, in that drifting in order to build up boost is the main thing you have to worry about when you aren’t dodging items. There’s also a new charge jump mechanic on top of that, which enables the player to grind on rails or even ride along walls, two things that _also_ build up boost if you do them right.

I haven’t even really scratched the surface of the kinds of shortcut opportunities that surely exist if you get good enough at those moves, but just knowing that there’s more depth here than before is enough for me. Pulling off a sick wallride feels great, if nothing else.

All of this works in concert with the true greatness of the Knockout Tour mode to create something I’m going to casually play online for many, many dozens of hours. It’s truly exciting to win a Knockout Tour in a way it’s never been to win in _Mario Kart_ before. Every time I finish in first place in an online Knockout Tour, I feel like I can take on God.

_Mario Kart World_ is an excellent Switch 2 showcase
----------------------------------------------------

![Image 9: Water in Mario Kart World](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-5.fill.size_2000x1125.v1749757157.png)

The water is gorgeous. Credit: Nintendo

One very important aspect of _Mario Kart World_ that maybe doesn’t come through until you see it running on a 4K TV with HDR turned on is that it’s one of the best-looking games of 2025 so far. The Switch 2’s big boost in horsepower over its predecessor, combined with Nintendo’s excellent-as-usual art direction, make it an absolute delight to look at pretty much at all times.

_Mario Kart World_ is vibrant, colorful, and full of fun little details. Karts and racers bend and contort in cartoonish ways when they take hits, explosions now have comic book-esque “KABOOM!” text callouts on top of them, and the water, oh my _god_, the water. I think _Mario Kart World_ might have the best-looking water I’ve seen in a video game. It needs to be seen to be believed.

Aside from _World_’s prowess as a technical showcase, it’s also a great demonstrator of the Switch 2’s neat [online social features](https://mashable.com/article/nintendo-switch-2-gamechat-actually-great). I’ve had a ton of fun doing online races and Knockout Tours against friends while we casually hang out and talk about whatever is happening in our lives via GameChat. _World_ is an incredible hangout game, if nothing else.

But there are some gaps in the online feature set
-------------------------------------------------

![Image 10: Princess Rosalina in mario kart world race](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/02W92YuxiVcA1DiBrKNiLKC/images-7.fill.size_2000x1124.v1749859111.png)

Also gorgeous. Credit: Nintendo

Unfortunately, the online features could be a bit more fleshed out in a couple of ways.

First, free roaming around the open world with friends appears to be limited to driving around while waiting for races or Knockout Tours to start. The P-switch challenges are removed from the open world when playing this way, turning it into a glorified lobby rather than a true, cooperative open world. I wish there was more to do in the open world in general, but I think this sentiment is especially true of the online version of it.

Secondly, I wish you could queue up for online Knockout Tour races against random strangers while partied up with your friends. Instead, to do an online Knockout Tour with friends, you either need to find 23 other people (unlikely) or accept that some of the slots will be filled with NPC characters. I think this is a fantastic online game in many ways, but it’s not always ideal.

Is _Mario Kart World_ worth it?
-------------------------------

Look, everyone has their own idea of what a dollar is worth, or in this case, 80 of them. I think _Mario Kart World_ is a great game and [I would pay $80 for it if I had to](https://mashable.com/article/mario-kart-world-price-concerns-switch-2), but I’m also comically irresponsible with money.

Moving past the value proposition of it all, _World_ is just a ton of fun. It’s fun to look at, fun to win at, and even fun to lose at, if your mindset is properly attuned to it.

![Image 1: MarioKartWorld_Intro_Sideimg_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

### Start your engines and race across a sprawling world!

Hit the open road with Mario and friends! Zip along courses on a vast world where everything is connected. Race around grassy plains, bustling cities, wide-open waters, big ol' volcanos, and more...plus everything in-between. Exclusively for [Nintendo Switch 2](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Hardware/Nintendo-Switch-2/Nintendo-Switch-2-2785301.html "Nintendo Switch 2")!

![Image 2: MarioKartWorld_Intro_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 3: MarioKartWorld_World_Headline_EN.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

#### World

##### Everywhere is your race course!

![Image 4: MarioKartWorld_World_Map_Full.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 5: MarioKartWorld_World_Sideimg_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

A sprawling world of courses
----------------------------

Speed across plains, cities, water, volcanos, and much more. Everything is connected!

![Image 6: MarioKartWorld_World_Map_Inner.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 7: MarioKartWorld_World_Map_Stages.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 8: MarioKartWorld_World_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Go beyond the course
--------------------

There's more to racing than just the road. Hop off the course and race the distance to the next one!

![Image 9: MarioKartWorld_Modes_Sideimg.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 10: MarioKartWorld_Modes_Headline_EN_NL.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

#### Races

### Burn rubber in heated 24-driver races!

Grand Prix
----------

Grand Prix
----------

Compete to earn the most points across four connected courses. Try to claim the top spot among 24 racers!

The areas between courses are part of the race, too!

Compete to earn the most points across four connected courses. Try to claim the top spot among 24 racers!

The areas between courses are part of the race, too!

### A non-stop transcontinental rally

Knockout Tour
-------------

Barrel through back-to-back courses, with no pit stops along the way!

If you don't place high enough by the time you reach each of the five checkpoints…you're OUT.

Drive hard to survive and aim for first place!

Barrel through back-to-back courses, with no pit stops along the way!

If you don't place high enough by the time you reach each of the five checkpoints…you're OUT.

Drive hard to survive and aim for first place!

![Image 12: MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Headline_EN.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

#### Free Roam

### Drive wherever your heart takes you!

Where to? That's up to you! Take off in any direction in this new mode. Explore areas that pique your interest, and maybe even snap some pics at scenic spots.

![Image 13: MarioKartWorld_Racer_Mario.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 14: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Headline_EN.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

#### Drivers and Vehicles

Race as familiar favourites and surprising additions, with so many combinations of drivers, vehicles and outfits to discover!

![Image 15: MarioKartWorld_Item_Sideimg_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 16: MarioKartWorld_Item_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Check out the new skills and items that'll give you a competitive edge on the course!

![Image 20: MarioKartWorld_Play_Headline_EN.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

#### Play together

##### Have a blast with friends, whether near or far!

Up to four players can race on the same console
-----------------------------------------------

![Image 21: MarioKartWorld_Play_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Play using your choice of button controls or motion controls. Attach a Joy-Con 2 controller to the Joy-Con 2 wheel accessory (sold separately) to wheely feel like you're driving.

You can also play using Nintendo Switch Joy-Con controllers connected wirelessly.

![Image 22: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Place your face in the race!
----------------------------

![Image 23: MarioKartWorld_Play_Scr_04.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

![Image 24: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

With CameraPlay, you can connect a compatible USB-C camera, such as the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), to see each others' reactions while you play! CameraPlay works with everyone gathered together in the same room or over GameChat.

![Image 25: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Note: Video features require a compatible USB-C camera (sold separately).

All together, anytime, anywhere
-------------------------------

![Image 26: MarioKartWorld_Play_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Fire up GameChat to enjoy the feeling of close company with friends – even when you're far apart!

![Image 27: MarioKartWorld_Play_Scr_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/01_website_elements/other_elements/grey.gif)

Talk using the console's built-in microphone or share your screen in real time. If you connect a compatible USB-C camera, like the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), you can go face-to-face over video chat.

Whether you're competing in a race or simply exploring the open road, it's like you're zooming around together!

To use online services, you must create a Nintendo Account and accept the related agreement. The Nintendo Account Privacy Policy applies. Internet connection and paid Nintendo Switch Online membership required. Mobile phone number registration required to use GameChat. Children must get approval from a parent or guardian via the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app to use GameChat. Some online services may not be available in all countries. A compatible USB-C camera, such as the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), is required to use some game features and video chat.

Until March 31st 2026, anyone can enjoy GameChat! Afterwards, a Nintendo Switch Online membership will be required.
